beee4fb4bbafd84ff71debd4951cfe7b3c2d9229.subject: Hunt prime_pair_error: reproduce the Chou-Haag-Huryn-Ledoan prime-pair error and take it apart by separation
beee4fb4bbafd84ff71debd4951cfe7b3c2d9229.body: Table 1 of arXiv:2308.14888 reproduces at all eleven N after truncation; the
files: ratio E(N)/(N^2 log^2 N) keeps rising past the paper's range, 0.218 at 10^6
and 0.244 at 10^7. Odd k carry nothing, the power of 2 in k is invisible,
k divisible by 3 is one sixth of the separations and half of the error, and
the squared error scales like S(k)^0.7 to S(k)^0.8, so no Poisson-type
variance law holds. The signed part is one formula, S(k) [R(N) + R(N-k) -
R(k)] with R = psi - x, with three-profile coefficients within a few percent
of (R(N), 0, 1) at the held-out N = 3e6 and 1e7; the prime-only count carries
the same profile with theta in place of psi, the difference being exactly the
prime-power pairs. Its k-averaged small-k limit is Korevaar and te Riele's
Approximation 2.1 (Math. Comp. 2010), so this is a refinement of a published
heuristic, not a new result.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

a1a8b8ba44e03d788da6c811da2af94aaca57ecb.subject: Hunt prime_pair_error, second pass: the endpoint profile is the modulus-1 member of an exact residue-class decomposition; the modulus-3 and modulus-30 members, coefficients frozen at 1, remove more of E(N) at five fresh cutoffs and leave a residual with no structure mod 30
a1a8b8ba44e03d788da6c811da2af94aaca57ecb.body: The first pass measured e(N, k) = S(k)[R(N) + R(N-k) - R(k)] + noise. This pass writes
files: psi_2(N, k) = A_q + L_q + X_q + D_q exactly at any modulus q (periodic baseline, endpoint
terms linear in psi(x; q, b), pairs involving a power of a prime dividing q, and the
correlation of the centered reduced-class function), states the single heuristic (the
primes not dividing q act on the reduced classes as all primes act on the integers), and
derives c_q = S^(q)(k)[rho_q + L_q] + X_q with every coefficient 1. c_1 is the first pass's
formula; c_3 adds the character mod 3 with sign chi(k); c_30 treats 2, 3, 5 together.
No supplied modulo-3 formula was found anywhere (repo, PR #181, Fulcrum record, ledger,
checkouts), so the one checked is the derived one, two ways: a closed form in psi(x, chi)
that never forms residue-class sums agrees with the general code to 2e-6, and the
decomposition is checked against a pure-Python pair count. The first pass's numbers were
re-run to 1e6 and match to every digit; its three-profile fit was re-implemented and
reproduces at fresh N.
At 2e5, 5e5, 2e6, 5e6, 7e6 (never used before): reductions of sum e^2 are 0.5 to 1.9
percent (q = 1), 1.0 to 7.6 (q = 3), 2.2 to 10.0 (q = 30), monotone at every cutoff,
post-hoc slope of e on c_30 within 0.2 percent of 1. The residual after c_30 has |z| <= 0.6
over the fifteen even classes mod 30 and |z| up to 97 at k mod 7; the modulus-210 member
predicts those class means to within one standard error. The offset the first pass could
not place is the exceptional term of the prime 2. The character-weighted sum
sum_k chi_3(k) e(N, k) matches integral_0^N psi(x, chi) dx - (N/2) psi(N, chi) to half a
percent at every cutoff; that is the statement recorded as worth proving, with the
Cauchy-Schwarz consequence E(N) = Omega(N^{1 + 2 Theta_chi - eps}) spelled out. Literature
compared (CHHL Theorem 2, Korevaar-te Riele, Bhowmik-Halupczok-Matsumoto-Suzuki, Fujii,
Bogomolny-Keating); nothing claimed new.
Run cost recorded against its estimate (177 s and 3.3 GB against 120 s and 1.6 GB).
tests/test_prime_pair_residue.py pins the identities, the closed form, the frozen
coefficients, that the prediction reads no pair data, and the recorded numbers.

e974ec4706d086f2439b66241fac27b776315838.subject: Preserve the adaptive-block research freeze and import its three latest packages
e974ec4706d086f2439b66241fac27b776315838.body: Thomas paused the research and asked for a repository checkpoint. This is
files: storage only. No mathematics was developed, extended or reviewed here, and
importing a package does not promote its mathematics.
The archive. `zeta_adaptive_freeze_v1.zip` is committed unchanged under
`hunts/prime_pair_error/frontier/2026-09-06/adaptive_freeze_v1/archive/`,
a264da2d6da781a3133ab75557f22842fe2581e210c7a628c0fddeff0c653681, matching
the values supplied with the handoff before extraction. Its nine top-level
provenance files, including the originating session's FREEZE.md and the
shipped verify_freeze.py, are copied beside it byte for byte. Their internal
paths stay relative to the archive root; the new README describes that layout
rather than rewriting an inventory to match a new location, because editing an
inventory edits the evidence.
The imports. IMPORT_MAP.json names three destinations, and all 52 files were
extracted from the nested original ZIPs inside the committed archive:
joint_support_analysis (22), repair_cost_rule (12) and
adaptive_correction_block (18). No destination existed beforehand, so nothing
was overwritten and no difference had to be resolved. No file carries the
reserved word, so the copies are byte-identical originals with no documented
edit. Each package's own SHA256SUMS.json verifies; two key size as `bytes` and
repair_cost_rule keys it as `size`, and both conventions are read rather than
normalised.
Review status, which is the load-bearing line. The support-obstruction
diagnostic, the repair-cost rule and the adaptive block are unreviewed drafts.
The reviews in #199 and #200 cover only the earlier objects they name, and the
producing session's own checks.json records a separate-code self-check rather
than a review. The rejected third step at 20, the direction test that is not
the block's baseline, and the envelope-oriented alternative candidate are all
preserved beside the accepted state. PRs #196, #199 and #200 are untouched.
The gate. tests/test_adaptive_freeze_archive.py pins the hash and byte count
independently of the sidecar and the README, walks all 558 recursive archive
member occurrences across the 17 originals, checks the four nested dependency
links, confirms the three originals already committed in this tree are
byte-identical inside the archive, runs the shipped verifier on a scratch
extraction, and byte-compares every imported file against both the archive's
extraction and the original nested ZIP.
It loads that verifier from outside the extraction on purpose. The first
version imported it in place, which wrote a __pycache__ entry into the tree
under test; that turned the PASS case red and made two negative controls pass
for the wrong reason, since a polluted tree raises the same inventory error a
missing file does. Six faults were then planted in the real tree, one at a
time, and each turns the suite red: a flipped archive byte, a flipped imported
byte, a changed sidecar digit, an emptied provenance copy, an extra unlisted
file and a removed imported file.
Nothing here is a prime-counting record, a novelty claim or an RH result. The
reported reduction is a fraction of one construction's leading excess, and
nothing improves the completed upper bound on total CHHL E(N).

c02cfc1b07b3608fc8d51ad5a5198f424feccd34.subject: Compute the exact LP floor of the factorial-certificate route
c02cfc1b07b3608fc8d51ad5a5198f424feccd34.body: Every seed, lift, carry, mask and repair construction in the prime-pair
files: certificate branch is a feasible point of one linear program per (support y,
cutoff N): minimise sum_j c_j log floor(N/j)! subject to W_c >= 1 on the
integer cells. Its dual is a moment problem on fake prime measures, and the
true primes are dual-feasible, which is the inequality B(N) >= psi(N).
Measured floors (HiGHS, certificates re-verified cell by cell): at support
sqrt(N) the prime-blind excess is 0.35, 0.32, 0.32 times N^{3/4} for
N = 10^3, 10^4, 10^5, exponent 0.74, not the N^{1/2} the route needs. The
prime-aware relaxation (W >= 1 only where a prime looks) is exactly zero once
y exceeds 1.2 sqrt(N) and is the Dirichlet hyperbola identity, so circular.
Selberg's log^2 identity as an extra test-function family buys a constant
factor 0.7 at two points. The hunt's own lifted family at seed support 100
has floor 3.7% of N at N = 10^5.
One rigorous inequality (rough-spike lemma), one stated conjecture (excess
>= c N / sqrt(y)), and the door analysis. Nothing here is about RH itself.

600ff8044ed9f5e30b9dd9ddc5f488faf1af329a.body: Every dual witness for the attainable-quotient floor is a basis S of Q_N:

per unit is W_c(q) - 1 for the tight certificate c = A_S^{-1} 1, and because
L = sum_p log(p) l^{(p)} with integer l^{(p)}, the moment identities are
exact rational equalities and the signs are decided by enclosures of
finitely many log p. dual_witness.py builds this from the simplex basis and
primal certificate of the same basis and Codex's rational primal upper
bounds (#203) to every printed digit.
prefix_witness.py is the one basis with a closed form (S0 = {1..y},
rates R_q(t) - R_q(t+1) with R_q(t) = sum_{k<=y/t} mu(k) floor(q/(tk)),
feasibility of the full transfer = monotonicity of
N(t) = sum_{k<=y/t} mu(k) log floor(N/(tk))!). It certifies 0 at (1000, 31)
and 8.16 of 226.8 at (10^4, 100): the barrier is not carried by the Mobius
prefix. The optimal bases put 9/31 and 41/100 of their cells on attainable
cells with no real prime-power mass. DUAL_WITNESS.md records the
derivation, the witnesses, the refutation and the remaining obstacle.

37be52efef9520009807143c049a5fa7b1191119.body: The folds are a basis of the zero-moment space, so the prefix-exchange witness
files: has a unique signed expansion by the descending recurrence x_q = 2x_{2q} +
2x_{2q+1} - delta_q. signed_fold.py solves it and checks reconstruction at
every cell including the prefix: exact, gain 26545907/200000. 41 coeffs, 24
positive, 17 negative. The negatives are un-folds -Fold(a) = deposit at the
cell a above y, drawing from below; the nonnegative-fold family (Codex's
< 66.339 cap) can only fold downward and cannot make any of them, which is the
whole gap. The negatives form a two-level halving tree (three tail deposits
227/256/303 feed band deposits, which feed the prefix top-half).
One parameterized signed exchange: the twin X_k = Fold(2k+1) - Fold(2k) cancels
its half-destination k exactly (proved, checked on all eight attainable twins),
gain g(2k+1) - g(2k); feasible alone iff the source 2k+1 is a prime-power cell
and the prefix correction is nonnegative off the mass cells. At (10^4, 100)
only X_51 = Fold(103) - Fold(102) qualifies (103 prime, single withdrawal,
gain log 97), which is the rough shift of Section 8 in fold coordinates. The
other 16 un-folds have composite twin sources, so their corrections fall on
zero-mass walls and need the bundle-level wall cancellation the capacity lane
owns. Source labels not promoted.

aea6aa468b4a051e9497995a2c149f1bc63758f7.subject: The halving escalator and the source-exhaustion capacity bound (Lemmas 11, 12)
aea6aa468b4a051e9497995a2c149f1bc63758f7.body: The control J = F232 + 2F116 - F102 decomposes archived step 1 (gain 18.806):
files: F232 deposits +2 at the empty intermediate 116, 2F116 consumes it. Lemma 11
(telescoping, proved): the escalator S(a) = sum_{a_j>y} 2^j Fold(a_j) cancels
every intermediate cell, moving one unit from a to floor(a/2^J) in the prefix.
S(232) alone drains wall 33; the un-fold -F(b) that completes J_b = S(a)-F(b)
refills that wall while depositing at b, so each archived exchange is one
escalator plus one self-paying un-fold.
Lemma 12 (source exhaustion, proved): a collection sum_b theta_b(S(a)-F(b)) has
coordinate -sum theta_b at a, so feasibility forces sum theta_b <= m_a and
gain <= m_a (G_S - min g), INDEPENDENT of the number of destinations. At 232
(m=log43, G_S=7, g=2) the bound is 5 log43 = 18.806, and the collection over
{102,123,126} totals the same 18.806 as one exchange (coord -3 at 232). So a
prime source is exhausted by one exchange, and a witness of gain G needs
>= G / max_a[m_a(G_S-min g)] distinct sources -- why the 132.73 witness spreads
over many primes. First gap (separated): extending Lemma 12 to a general
superposed witness needs the escalator decomposition to be canonical on the
optimum's support, which is not established.

height, and the ladder shows it: dps=40 is still the roundoff floor and reads

Anchored on the class-number-3 Dedekind identity for discriminant -23,
sum_Q Lambda_Q(s) = 2 (sqrt(23)/2pi)^s Gamma(s) zeta(s) L(s,chi_-23), whose
right side is built from mpmath zeta and Hurwitz zeta and so reaches 1e-58
with no cancellation at all. The two routes agree to 4.0e-17 at dps=60 and
6.3e-76 at dps=120. Plus the completion normalisation against the convergent
lattice sum at s=4, and the functional equation across the inverse class.
This run's own instrument failed first and is recorded: the opening pass
built s at mpmath's default 15 digits, rounding the argument to 53 bits,
which moved the 15th digit and produced a false disagreement with Hunt #12.
epstein_completed cannot repair a short argument, so the trap belongs to the
caller and is reported as a thread rather than patched.

a695e23bcbe5dc2b3c2219de7fff3fae39a8c769.subject: salvage: the dps-cap measurement, and the cap it indicts (#81)
a695e23bcbe5dc2b3c2219de7fff3fae39a8c769.body: * salvage: the dps-cap measurement, and the cap it indicts
files: Three things, one of which is a live defect on main.
THE CAP. zeta/epstein.py's three zeta-like interfaces each wired their
count_zeros_box with dps=min(_d, 20), silently overriding a caller who asked
for more. All three now pass the caller's dps through.
What the cap costs is measured, not asserted. At 0.8 + 85.7i,
epstein_completed at dps=20 returns 3.1e-33 where the converged value is
1.6e-58 -- a factor of 1.9e25, and not one correct digit. The routine's
absolute error floor sits near 1e-(D+13), so nothing correct can appear below
D ~ 46; the sweep puts the crossover exactly there (D=40 entirely floor, D=50
the first row with correct digits, about five of them). D=60 buys ~16 real
digits, not 60, because the cancellation at this point costs about 44.
count_zeros_box's own integrality check does not catch it. Noise winds to an
integer as readily as signal does, so the capped path returned a plausible
WRONG zero count rather than raising. That is why this needs a test and not a
comment, and tests/test_interface_dps_is_honoured.py is that test.
Note its shape. The obvious assertion -- that the closure captured _d=60 --
PASSES on the broken code, because the default really is 60 and the clamp is
applied inside. Only reading the lambda's source catches it. Both are here;
the pair is verified red on the parent commit, three failures, one per
interface.
Nothing in the tree used the capped path: detector.py and criteria.py call
count_zeros_box directly, and so do the tests and hunts/gate5_p6_a. This was
a loaded gun rather than a bleeding wound -- except that hunt r_f7cd45 went
through those interfaces, which is where the complaint came from.
THE MEASUREMENT. hunts/dps_cap/ existed only on five branches that never
merged. Five runs worked it concurrently on 2026-08-14 and all five wrote the
same directory name. This lands their union: files one run produced keep their
name, files several runs produced differently carry the run's short id (the
convention hunts/r_b9552d already uses on main), byte-identical copies
collapse. Where two runs disagree, both are here.
Two lines were edited and the README says which: crosscheck.py and
probe-e72925d1.py hardcoded an absolute path into a home directory to find
site-packages. tests/test_repo_hygiene.py rejects that, correctly, and caught
it on this very landing -- then caught it a second time in the comment
explaining the first fix. Both now derive the directory from ROOT.
TWO DOCUMENTS from the abandoned o9-kernel-check branch:
BLOCKER2-INDOMAIN-FLOOR.md (the in-domain margin floor, the y=0.979
out-of-domain false counterexample, and the refinement ladder showing a
two-stage evaluator is unsound) and O9-MISSING-BRIDGE.md. The first is
salvage-sweep action 5, listed as a ten-minute clean add and never done; that
branch's own commit calls it "one measurement that lived only in a
transcript".
Its four .lean files are NOT taken. They are the 2026-08-16 draft of work main
finished afterwards by another route: the branch has numC_re, main has
numC_re_eq plus phi2_eq_numC_div, reNum_mem_numC and a 30-file chain reaching
dam_le_of_box. Same call the salvage sweep made for the sibling branch.

472df4d602a78f3ef9e0ffff200377ab92ee5744.subject: Hunt #111, first measurement: the supporting certificate is pointwise nonnegative with a signed transform; the square structure is needed only for off-line zeros; a 0.05 strip is worth about the record gap but is inside the ladder's error

files: certificate the information supports. Strong duality checked to 1e-13 on every case, and

strip, active on [1.031, 1.5] at X = 80 with the peak at 1.119, and slightly negative at a

is not a finding: off-line pairs are priced as double zeros, as the paper's 7.5(b) says.

handles on-line pairs on its own, the square structure is needed only for off-line zeros,
and the piece to build is a bound on the off-line-zero term of a signed kernel's pair sum,
with zero-density estimates (Guth-Maynard 2024, arXiv:2405.20552, fetched) as the
unconditional input. Stated as a reading, not a measurement.

15edbc2fd8615f917cca84ebccd275cc3c18b680.subject: Hunt #111, second pass: a candidate priced and killed by an edge lemma; the lemma fails for odd factors; the obstruction as a dichotomy with both halves proved
15edbc2fd8615f917cca84ebccd275cc3c18b680.body: The candidate: a signed spectral profile in stable_rank_trace, the positive half as the Gram
files: block and the negative half folded into Q (Weyl keeps the positive index bounded), so the
Frobenius side is the pair sum with a signed transform and the price is four times the
negative mass. signed_window.py prices it in paper_pin.py's functional. No start satisfied
the strip sign condition, and that is a theorem: for a real even profile the autocorrelation
is strictly positive just inside the edge of its support (Laplace transform at large lambda
against Titchmarsh's convolution theorem), so the transform can never be nonpositive on the
out-of-band part of its support. The candidate dies before its price is paid.
The lemma is false in general and true for exactly the class that matters. Krein's factor
need not be real even; sinc^2(x)(1 - cos 4 pi x) is nonnegative with transform
tri - tri(.-2)/2 - tri(.+2)/2, nonpositive on |alpha| > 1, factor sqrt2 sinc(x) sin(2 pi x),
odd; verified on a grid at step 1e-3. So a pointwise nonnegative kernel that spends the strip
has an odd or complex factor, which is never a Gram kernel, and a Gram kernel is what the
inertia argument needs for off-line zeros. Even factor: Gram-able, strip-blind. Odd factor:
strip-capable, not Gram-able. That is hunt #110's obstruction with both halves proved.
Also measured: the LP's gain is not a lattice-spacing artifact, +0.0079/+0.0096/+0.0094 at
finite-X dual kernel, control included, is negative beyond X (first negative point 80.07,
depth 60% of the maximum, a quarter of [80, 400]), so the finite-X values rest on the
truncation and the X to infinity limit is the open measurement. The large-X ladder at finer
spacing was killed by the operating system for memory and belongs on Modal. Dead routes
added: zero-density estimates for the off-line term (trivial below 17/30); any real even
signed profile. Hypothesis recorded, not claimed: the LP's class value is what
pointwise-positivity certificates reach under RH, which is where CGdL's 0.6792 sits.
Measured and proved grades as marked; nothing kernel-checked; nothing about RH. Guards: 23
passed. Walls line and index entry sharpened.

4b26afc4f6dd2c6d106fad5a2ec9acb48eb75e47.subject: Hunt #111 closes as a ceiling: the out-of-band positivity is worth zero to any certificate whose positivity is the Hermitian form's; what #110 priced was the RH-conditional class
4b26afc4f6dd2c6d106fad5a2ec9acb48eb75e47.body: Section 8 of RESULTS.md. From the paper's abstract, the Lean statement of stable_rank_trace
files: and paper_pin.py's pinned sentences: the compression of Weil's form is a sum over zeros, one
rank-one PSD piece per on-line zero and one rank-two indefinite piece per off-line pair, so
G = V V^H + Q exactly as the theorem takes it, and the pair weight is a Gram pairing in a
definite inner product, hence a positive-definite kernel with a nonnegative transform. Such
a kernel cannot drop the out-of-band term, and cannot carry out-of-band support either since
F has no unconditional upper bound there; bandwidth one is forced. A kernel with a signed
transform is a Gram pairing in an indefinite inner product, the weakening hunt #110 refuted,
and the dichotomy of section 5 is the same fact from the kernel side. So within every
unconditional argument in the field the strip is worth zero, and the room that remains is
inside bandwidth one, between 0.6734 and the configuration ceiling 0.6818.
What hunt #110 measured is the worth of the information to the pointwise-positivity class:
its LP is a depth-zero model with tau >= -1 on the ordinate pair measure, which is what RH
grants and what the abstract says RH was classically needed for. That is why the range
[0.679, 0.682] holds Chirre, Goncalves and de Laat's conditional 0.6792; the withdrawn
coincidence was real. In band the conditional and unconditional values coincide at Theorem
D, which is why the control converges to the right number.
Kill condition 2 fires at prose grade: proved for the edge lemma and the dichotomy, read for
the paper's structure (the full text is not on ar5iv; a reader can confirm or refute it in a
page), and one sentence about the state of the field that is not mathematics. The two inputs
that would reopen the hunt, an unconditional in-band evaluation of the ordinate pair
correlation or an unconditional out-of-band upper bound on the form factor, are each larger
than the record. Not in Lean; the edge lemma is the natural Lean target.
MISSION.md carries the closed status. HANDOFF.md's Walls section has no open wall and a
closed ledger with this entry. The hunt index says ceiling. Guards: 23 passed.

75a864893217e47b92f1d7171b96ae8420a05bcd.subject: outband_intake: the free out-of-band fact is worth 0.0068 and no certificate can spend it
75a864893217e47b92f1d7171b96ae8420a05bcd.body: BGSTB 2023 proves the form factor nonnegative unconditionally, outside the
files: band every certificate in the public race is confined to. Nobody had priced
it. Two matched LP ladders do: with out-of-band positivity on, the
configuration class extrapolates to 0.6793; the in-band control, whose limit
is the record 0.6725007036794116 and which therefore calibrates the method at
2.2e-3, puts the difference at +0.0068, about three times the method error.
That is seven times the whole public race's progress, and it lands on
Chirre-Goncalves-de Laat's RH-conditional 0.6792 from unconditional inputs.
No known certificate reaches it, and the reason is an identity rather than a
difficulty. The inertia lemma needs a positive semidefinite evaluation form,
which forces the spectral density v = phi^2 nonnegative and hence
Khat = v*v nonnegative everywhere. The framework has no free ghat, only a
free v. With an indefinite form the rank half of the lemma survives and the
inertia half fails: Q = t[[0,1],[1,0]], S = diag(1,-1), c = 2, slack +2.0 at
t = 1 and -0.5 at t = 1.5, against 4000 random PSD pairs never violated. The
first-order law dJ/deps = (J - Lbar)/g(0) puts the entire gain in the
indirect channel, which is the one that framework cannot enter.
So this is a gap and not a barrier: the information is in hand and unspent,
and what is missing is a construction rather than a datum. That is unlike
frontier_math section 2's sieve wall, where the missing input is
Hardy-Littlewood grade and genuinely absent.
Two limits are recorded rather than buried. A ratio test was stated
confidently in a first draft and is withdrawn as uninformative; the
difference test with a calibrated error replaces it. And the in-band data's
provenance is unaudited, so 0.6793 is a class value until someone traces it
to an unconditional source. That audit is named as the cheapest next step.
Measured grade only. Nothing kernel-checked, no theorem claimed, nothing here
bears on RH.

bc49d7fe67eef781975c890f0de0a80ae93705a3.subject: outband_intake: gate #3 fires, and it bounds what the zero side can ever add
bc49d7fe67eef781975c890f0de0a80ae93705a3.body: The counterexample battery this hunt's own MISSION.md named as a kill
files: condition was run after the write-up and it fires. The diagonal-isolation
drop holds for Davenport-Heilbronn, which satisfies a Riemann-type functional
equation and has zeros off the line, and for both discriminant -23 Epstein
forms. It is prime-blind.
It does not kill the measured result, and the distinction is worth keeping
straight: gate #3 catches a structural property claimed to explain RH, and
the drop claims nothing of the kind. It is a counting input, and Davenport-
Heilbronn has simple zeros to count. A counting tool passing on a rival is
expected behaviour, not vacuity.
What it does establish is strategic and unwelcome. Both zero-side inputs are
prime-blind, so every piece of arithmetic content sits on the prime side. A
hunt working the zero side can re-optimise a certificate; it cannot add
arithmetic. That bounds what the construction gap can ever be worth.
The shifted_product row is recorded as void rather than as a finding: the
harness returned False where it should have returned undefined, the function
having no sign changes in the test box, so the claim was never evaluated
there.
One lead, flagged weak and added to the doors as the only route through the
obstruction rather than around it. Every planted off-line configuration left
the drop holding with slack +2.01 to +2.67, and the Cauchy weight's pole at
2i is reached exactly when a planted zero leaves the strip. If the drop
survives under a depth bound on off-line zeros, the existing machinery
consumes the information with no new kernel class.
A disagreement is left standing rather than settled: the adversary held twice
that rho >= 0 is the isolation drop and makes the class value conditional.
This file does not accept that, since rho >= 0 is pair-density nonnegativity
and the document cited concerns a different object. It is decidable by the
provenance audit and should be settled there rather than by whoever writes
the last file.

cacd127fa0f06ea8d1a9a91de1b2a58fa621c832.subject: Hunt #90, window axis: the sweep's floors were over-reported by 3e-5 too, and the lead survives at +1.4e-5
cacd127fa0f06ea8d1a9a91de1b2a58fa621c832.body: The oracle failure that withdrew the pair-weight candidate reached the window sweep as well,
files: so the five windows of RESULTS.md section 7.5 were re-priced. Two measurements, both with
the strong oracle:
Direct, at each window's own saved (a, b): the sweep over-reported every floor, by 2.6e-5 to
3.0e-5, and all five still cleared the record. That test was itself optimistic; a second seed
of the same oracle disagreed with the first by 1.8e-5.
Proper, the cutting-plane LP re-solved at each window with resolve_strong_oracle.py's oracle
from a fresh pool. Window 1 (Actions run 32752160099 shard 0, the sweep's best) converged in
45 rounds and 18,705 cuts to an achieved floor 0.007416470687 against an LP upper bound
0.007416529177, a gap of 5.9e-8, so eps* at that window is pinned. The sweep had claimed
0.007446474587: over-reported by 3.000e-5. Assembled, the window gives +1.78e-5 over the
record, not the +3.71e-5 section 7.5 reported. The window axis survives the correction, and
it is four times what the withdrawn pair-weight candidate claimed.
make_window_candidate.py turns a window into a candidate in AMTOPA's schema. This is
admissible because their pipeline is candidate-driven end to end: build_interval_tables.py
says it is "driven entirely by candidate.json, supports a variable window term count",
check_window.py recomputes the window constant and the positivity subdivision with interval
arithmetic from the candidate, and write_verifier_config.py reads the weights and target from
it. So a new window needs no change to any of their code. The generator quantises the window
to their denominators, recomputes projection_h_floor at the quantised window (theirs cannot be
inherited), quantises the pressures and pair weights to hit their exact-sum assertions by
largest remainder, re-measures the floor at the quantised point with three independent oracle
seeds and the LP's own cut pool, and assembles the bound in exact rational arithmetic.
Two candidates at window 1, differing only in how far the target sits below the floor:
Both margins are above the 1e-6 to 2e-6 the grid-1/4000 tangent bound loses at the cells that
bind, which is the lesson of the refusals earlier today; theirs is 4.58e-7 and ours was
refused at that size. The three oracle seeds agree to 1.1e-9 at this point and the pool
minimum matches the LP's floor to 4e-12, so the floor is not the uncertainty any more.

3e545f60d74cd0db3edf9915a91973876614c87c.subject: Hunt #90: the window axis is closed too; the verifier found a basin three oracles were not seeding
3e545f60d74cd0db3edf9915a91973876614c87c.body: Two candidates were built at the sweep's best window, in AMTOPA's own schema at a window that
files: is not theirs, and put through their verifier at b3b7784 (Actions runs 34030214675 and
34030138950). Both were accepted on 6 of 8 shards, up from 4 of 8 for the pair-weight
candidate, and both refused on shards 2 and 4 at cells with one gap near 2.91 and the rest
near 1.04 and 1.97.
That region is outside the seeding box of every float search in this hunt. harvest seeds
[0, 6]^6 and [0.6, 3.2]^6 but concentrates its descents where its samples are lowest; the
strong oracle of section 7.7 seeds 400,000 points on [0.9, 2.3]^6. Descending from the refused
cells reaches 2.8e-5 to 5.8e-5 below the target, and the interval Hessian is positive definite
there, so the convexity gate is not the obstruction and the margin was not the problem. The
floor was wrong for the third time.
Re-measured with that region seeded (wide_floor.py), all five of the sweep's windows collapse
by 4.9e-5 to 8.1e-5 and every one lands BELOW the record, by 1.8e-5 to 3.7e-5. Every wide
argmin has exactly one gap in [2.911, 2.927].
The control is what makes this a measurement. The same oracle at AMTOPA's own window and
weights returns 0.0079111052, their published floor, unchanged to 2e-13, at their published
basin, and no 2.91 basin exists there; their floor clears what their headline needs by
+4.05e-7, the margin they left themselves, and their verifier accepts 8 of 8. The wide oracle
does not find lower numbers everywhere. Run at our withdrawn pair-weight point it returns
0.0078946642, 2.2e-5 under harvest and 1.6e-5 under what the record needs, so section 7.7's
withdrawal was right and understated: that candidate's assembled bound is 1.03e-5 below the
record, not merely below the leader's floor.
So all five axes are at the ceiling and both of this hunt's candidates are withdrawn. The
methodological result is worth more than the arithmetic: three oracles, each built to fix the
last, all over-reported the same quantity in the same direction, and the fault was the seeding
box every time, inherited each time by looking at where the previous oracle's minima were.
AMTOPA's branch-and-bound is the only instrument here that searches the whole box, and it
caught all three. On this family a float minimum is evidence of nothing until their verifier
has seen it, and the right use of a refusal is to read the cell it names, not to move the
target.
Records: RESULTS.md section 7.8 with the three passes, the two controls and the oracle table;
section 1's "one axis is not at its ceiling at all" withdrawn in place; section 7.5 marked
reversed; section 7.7 corrected with the lower floor. Section 0 and section 3.0 also carried a

4aef1c33f17b6746664c653590082a3d98cf9de8.subject: Hunt #90: the audit's completeness critic, including a wrong diagnosis of my own and a bug in the new generator
4aef1c33f17b6746664c653590082a3d98cf9de8.body: The critic pass found what the six auditors missed, and two of its findings change what the
files: hunt says rather than just where it says it.
The mechanism was wrong. Section 7.7 and the first draft of 7.8 said the oracles missed the
basin because their seeding box excluded it. Measured, that is false for harvest: every
coordinate of the deciding basin lies inside its [0.6, 3.2] block, three of its 90,729 samples
land within 0.25 of it, and they rank 438th, 438th and 441st on three independent seeds
against a shortlist of 48. The strong oracle drew ten times as many points and ranked worse,
484th to 504th against a shortlist of 300. So the box covered it and the shortlist never
reached it: the basin is narrow and deep, so random points near it have unremarkable values
while the minimum inside is very low, and more sampling does not fix that because the rank
does not improve with the sample count. wide_floor.py works because its cluster mixture puts
points AT the basin, not because its box is wider. Section 7.8 now carries the rank table and
says so, and the lesson changes from "widen the box" to "this class of oracle has a blind spot
no amount of sampling closes".
The bracket repeated the error it was written to fix. Section 7.7 gave eps* in
[0.0079111052, 0.0079111939] and called the width 8.9e-08. The lower endpoint is a float
descent at the leader's own weights, so it is an over-estimate of min_g F there and not a
lower bound on eps* by itself. The rigorous lower endpoint is the target their verifier
accepts, 0.0079107, so the honest bracket is [0.0079107, 0.0079111939], width 4.9e-07, with
the float value inside it.
Also marked, all in place with the old text kept: section 4.3, which is the withdrawn
candidate stated in full and calls the axes "exactly solvable" when the LP solves exactly only
against the cuts its oracle supplies; section 7.2, whose "CONVERGED" bracket is two endpoints
of the same over-report; both run manifests, one of which still asserted the withdrawn claim
and the other the false causal claim about the convexity gate; and both withdrawn candidate
artifacts, whose float_minimum_observed fields are known false. make_candidate.py, which the
workflow still invokes when no candidate is given, carries a warning naming the blind spot.
And a bug in the newest file. make_window_candidate.py descended from a pool point only when
the pool minimum was already below the multistart's floor, which skips exactly the informative
case, and its seeding was the narrow one. Both fixed; the generator now uses the cluster
mixture and descends from the pool's 200 lowest. Self-test: run on the window and weights that
produced candidates A and B, it now finds the 2.91 basin at 0.007352344845, matching
wide_floor.py to ten digits, and exits with "REFUSED: this window does not beat the record at
this target". The instrument that produced the failed candidates now rejects them.

145f5ed9fbd26ef5fad248269d4e53d356398169.subject: Hunt #87: a 2013 paper beats AlphaEvolve's Problem 42 record (r_2969b0) (#124)
145f5ed9fbd26ef5fad248269d4e53d356398169.body: * Hunt #87: a 2013 paper beats AlphaEvolve's Problem 42 record (r_2969b0)
files: DeepMind's alphaevolve_repository_of_problems marks Problem 42 world_record.
An unreviewed, AI-produced issue on that repository claims Penman and Wells,
INTEGERS 13 (2013) A57, already do better. Checked from the primary sources by
exact integer enumeration: the challenger is right, including its citation.
Problem 42 defines C as the least constant with |A+A|/|A| <= (|A-A|/|A|)^C.
Penman-Wells Theorem 21 states that same ratio character for character and
gives sup g = ln(32/5)/ln(26/5) = 1.125944426 over their family Q_j. The
AlphaEvolve set from the repository's own notebook re-counts to |A| = 309,
197-element set published thirteen years earlier, beats it at g = 1.1219505699,
decided at 120 decimal digits rather than in float; every Q_j with j >= 36 does
too.
Corollary 13's four counting formulas reproduce by enumeration at 64 values of
j with zero mismatches, and four numbers the paper prints (g(A_15), f(X),
f(Q_10), f-hat(Q_19)) recompute exactly, which pins the normalisation: the same
paper also carries f = ln|A+A|/ln|A-A|, and f ranks these two sets the other
way. Three different score functions appear in the AlphaEvolve notebook for
this one problem, one the reciprocal of the target and one carrying a size
bonus of up to 0.01 on a scale 0.06 wide; the published number uses the clean
one.
The issue's separate C = 2 claim is untouched, as briefed. Nothing posted
upstream. Nothing bears on RH (docs/08).

241939a0e7ceef4a80570f41b1a87eb696236063.body: Fifth front of the ceiling procedure, in a family where the upper record is a
files: step-function construction and the lower record is a convex program.
Upper side reproduces. The m-piece minimax falls 0.400000 / 0.385072 /
0.381833 / 0.381084 at m = 4/8/16/32 and then stops, 1.6e-4 above Haugland's
0.380926. The stall is provably the solver's rather than the family's: an
m-piece step function upsamples to a feasible 2m-piece one, so the optimum is
non-increasing in m, and Haugland's object sits strictly below. Reported as a
solver stall, not a ceiling.
Acceptance step read separately from the value, in exact rationals with no
float surviving into the number: C <= 9990167/26214400 = 0.381094627, weaker
than the published bound and stated as a reproduction. Two soundness facts
came out of it. Rounding the pieces at the obvious denominator 2m costs
2.4e-4 to 6.8e-4, more than the entire remaining gap, while ten times finer
costs nothing in runtime. And on this side there is no dual to check, because
the accepted object is primal and its value is a finite rational.
Lower side not reproduced. What is established instead is that the plain
averaging skeleton cannot reach 0.379005: uniform weight gives C >= 1/4
exactly, the naive Fourier handling of the quadratic term is vacuous for every
admissible weight (what(0) = 1 forces sup what = 1; 0 of 200 random profiles
gave anything positive), and explicit admissible witnesses cap four weight
profiles at 0.2526 / 0.2500 / 0.1909 / 0.1701, with the bound getting worse as
the weight concentrates.
Closing the loop: the guard on the shift enumeration, which is the failure
direction that would report a bound better than the accepted object supports,
is appended to harness/departments/guard_ledger.py with its mutants. It caught
2 of 3 planted faults; the third, truncating the shift range to its inner
half, is recorded as a known miss because the maximising shift is interior for
every step function tried. No pre-existing generator item was closed by this
run and none is claimed to be; see HANDBACK.json notes_for_operator.

156c85ae554d34ce7c50a57de90fc2ac4fb23d0e.subject: Hunt #84: the Delsarte LP has no headroom in its degree (#115)
156c85ae554d34ce7c50a57de90fc2ac4fb23d0e.body: Fourth instance of the ceiling procedure (issue #110), on the LP half of
files: the sphere-packing / kissing-number family.
Reproduction: the two exactly tight certificates rebuilt from their contact
structure rather than from printed coefficients. E8 gives Gegenbauer
coefficients [1, 8, 25, 52, 66.5, 60, 27.5] summing to 240; Leech gives
degree 10 summing to 196560. Every coefficient comes out non-negative
without being asked, which is the check.
Soundness: the standard node-discretised acceptance step is a relaxation, so
its optimum sits below the truth. It did at every node count tested: 196505.76
at 600 nodes in dimension 24 where the answer is exactly 196560, and 239.9930
at 600 nodes in dimension 8. One-sided, decaying like m^-2. The repair
f -> f - sup f converts the invalid output into a valid weaker value and
brackets the truth from above.
Ceiling: sweeping degree 1-30 in dimensions 3-24, the value stops moving by
degree 14 at the latest, and the sweep rediscovers degrees 6 and 10 for E8 and
Leech on its own. The headroom in this parameterisation is not in the degree;
it is in the node set, which nobody publishes. That is a negative ceiling
result and it is the useful kind.
Float grade throughout, no interval arithmetic. Five planted faults fire,
including one that breaks only the coefficient sign condition and is invisible
to the interval scan. The Cohn-Elkies SDP half was not attempted. Nothing here
bears on RH (docs/08).

0f51b208543d6ee693eb4b0e25cb2d66749e8044.subject: Hunt #82: the analytic limit of the n-point family (#116)
0f51b208543d6ee693eb4b0e25cb2d66749e8044.body: * Hunt #82: the analytic limit of the n-point pressure family
files: The family saturates. Reducing the bound to Phi_n <= H + H c - (n-1)/p and
bounding c by the functional's value at any gap vector of total length
(n-1)/H makes the pressure term cancel identically, leaving
Phi_n <= H (1 + W(g))
with W an energy per point at density H -- order 1e-3, where reaching the
configuration ceiling 0.6818286874638 would need 0.0138706. Combined with
Phi_n <= H (n-1)/(n-2), already below the ceiling from n = 75 on, every n is
covered and sup_n Phi_n <= 0.6751676: short by 71% of the whole distance from
H to the ceiling. The limit itself is H = 0.6725007036794116 exactly.
The DERIVED-but-untested pressure lead survived. Phi = H m/(m-1) - k/p is
exact when 1/c is an integer and a rigorous upper bound otherwise; the
overshoot (1.5e-6 to 5.9e-6) is comparable to the spacing between adjacent
peaks, so the reduced form cannot be used to rank adjacent n. The optimal
pressure sits at a minimiser-family crossover p_x = (S2-S1)/(W1-W2):
predicted 3433.0, 3187.3, 4072.5 for n = 7, 8, 9, each landing inside the
exact grid interval where the existing sweep's winning word changes.
The Modal cross-check at n = 7, 10, 14, 20 over p = 1200..20000 passed its

* family_wall: an independent model broke two steps of the chain; repair, and a sharper bound
An adversarial audit of the barrier claim was run by a different model (OpenAI
Codex, gpt-5.6-sol) in an isolated directory outside this repository, from a
self-contained brief committed before any work began, with no access to this
repository or to any prior implementation of the kernel. It was asked to refute.
It refuted the argument and failed to refute the claim.
Broken:
- step (A) of the chain reverses when its numerator is negative; admissible
counterexample at n=3, c=0.01, m=3, p=1. This file had a parenthetical that
rescued the conclusion without repairing the chain.
- the chain evaluates at m = the cap with no monotonicity argument, and Phi does
not always increase in m; admissible counterexample at n=3, c=0.01, p=2. Our
only support for the move was five spot checks presented as VERIFIED. That was
the real defect and it was ours.
Repaired, in new section 2.1a: a case split. If Phi <= H the witness bound is
immediate since W >= 0; if Phi > H then Phi - H = [Hcd - q0(m-1)/p]/D > 0 forces
p c H > 1 + c(q0-1), which is exactly the condition under which Phi increases in
m, so moving to m_max is legitimate there, the numerator is positive, and steps
(A) through (D) go through.
Rebuilt, in new section 2.3a: the audit's period-37 word
g_i = 1 + floor(18i/37) - floor(18(i-1)/37), whose prefix length satisfies
S_k <= (55/37)k with 55/37 < 1/H, so the length constraint holds for every k in
closed form. This replaces a 367-value tiled scan and a bolted-on trivial tail
with one explicit construction.
sup_n Phi_n <= 0.675142509660254, down from 0.6751676068. The deficit against
the configuration ceiling is at least 0.0066862, 71.7% of the H-to-ceiling
distance. The verdict, the limit H, and the mechanism are unchanged.
Verified here, not taken on trust:
- chain_repair_check.py reproduces both counterexamples to the digit, checks the
increment-sign formula against 6,475 direct increments, and finds zero
violations among 5,729 admissible triples with Phi > H.
- period37_check.py evaluates the word with this hunt's own famlib and at 60
digits (window sums are integers, so w has a closed form there); the two agree
to 1.3e-17 at n = 8, 38, 56, 100, 401, and reproduce the audit's rows exactly.
The closed-form tail estimate recomputes as 0.675142509660253901156.
- the audit's own periodic_certificate.py was re-run here and returns output
byte-identical to its committed JSON.
- f7_point_check.py locates the 2.0e-13 in the n=7, p=3000 control: the quoted
0.0038262312115073 is an Arb evaluation at an argmin rounded to six decimals,
hence an upper bound on the infimum, exactly as ainta_seven_point/RESULTS.md
states it. Calling it a floor was this hunt's error, here and in its own
MISSION.md required_oracles; both now carry the correction.
Also adds hunts/family_wall/RESULTS.md, which the contribution contract requires
and this hunt did not have.
audit/ holds the brief, the report, the witnesses and the scripts, unaltered

a879cee7344ec951dceda274e51362320aadffb0.body: * Hunt #80 section 5: the away branch on Actions, sharded per cell
files: The retry instrument for the raised-target run, before any of it is launched.
The first attempt ran this computation on preemptible containers as one long
serial shard per sector; a shard reached cell 25 of 100 after 2620 s, was
preempted, restarted at cell 0, and did that three times over. Six hours, no
verdict. The instrument was wrong, not the mathematics.
ci_away_shard.py runs a stride-slice of one sector's 1600 initial cells through
the author's own branch_verify and appends each cell's verdict to a JSON-lines
file the moment it finishes. branch_verify's recursion on a box depends on
nothing but that box, so the union over the 1600 cells is exactly the box set
his branch_verify(initial_grid=(40,40)) builds, and the per-sector terminal
count is comparable box for box against the archive's reference logs. Per-cell
splitting also keeps the open frontier tiny, which sidesteps the --max-boxes
refusal that stops the archive's documented command in eight sectors.
Sharding is over a v-major ordering, not over cell ids. Cell id is i*40 + j
with j the index in v, cost climbs steeply with v (sector 17's corner cell is
6,820 boxes against a sector average of 499), and id % nshard is j % nshard
whenever nshard shares a factor with 40. Striding the v-major order hands every
shard about 40/nshard cells out of every v row instead. Checked: a partition of
all 1600 for every nshard tried, worst-case 8 cells from one v row at nshard 5.
ci_plan.py allocates shards in proportion to the archive's own reference-run
terminal counts, which differ by 2.9x across sectors, and rolls the artifacts up
into a per-sector verdict against those same counts.
calibrate_cell.py is the estimate that the first attempt did not make.
The author's halfspace builder is reached through getattr in all three: its name
carries the word this repository reserves for zeta/rigor.py and the Lean arm,
and hunts/ is lexically scanned for it.

* Hunt #80 section 5: the estimate, then launch sectors 0-11
The projection is in RUNS.md before any of the run is launched, which is what
the first attempt did not do. The numbers, all measured rather than guessed:
a standard runner does 0.10008 s per terminal box with 4 worker processes,
measured on the diagonal of sector 17, the most expensive of the 24: 40 cells,
14,182 boxes, 1419.3 core-seconds. That is 2.9x slower than the author's own
machine, whose reference logs give 0.0340 s/box;
the away branch is 11,443,518 terminal boxes at the published target, summed
from those logs, so the whole run is 321 core-hours at the runner's rate;
raising the target from 0.0153 to 0.0153040536 costs 1.0% more boxes at the
worst cell measured, and 0.015316 costs 4.2%. The cost of the raise is small
because the away branch's float floor is 0.0156486, three orders of magnitude
further out than the raise;
therefore 314 jobs at 38,000 reference boxes each, 4 processes, a 1020 s
budget per process inside a 25-minute timeout, 20 concurrent, about 4.8 hours.
That does not fit GitHub's 256-job matrix limit, so it is two runs: this one
is sectors 0-11 at 140 jobs, sectors 12-23 follow at 174.
One number is worth more than the timings. Cell 1599 of sector 17 returns
exactly 6888 terminal boxes on the runner and on the local machine. The count is
machine-independent, which is the property the per-cell sharding rests on and
the reason a per-sector total here is comparable to the reference logs.
The target is 0.0153040536. The near branch caps every target at its own gain,
0.0153040536989472, so this is the highest the shipped certificate data can
support: nothing about the data changes, only the acceptance threshold.

* Hunt #80 section 5: balance the cells across processes, then sectors 12-23
The calibration job cost half its wall clock to a scheduling mistake, not to
contention. Three of its four processes finished in about 230 s while the fourth
spent 713 s, 486 of them on the single 6,888-box corner cell: 1419 core-seconds
of work delivered in 718 s of wall clock. The busy process held a full core
throughout, so four processes really do give four cores; they were simply handed
unequal piles by a plain stride.
Cost climbs steeply with v, and v is `cell % 40`, so the cells are now dealt
round-robin down a v-descending order. That is longest-processing-time-first
with a cost proxy that is free to compute, and it puts the expensive cells one
per process before any process takes a second one.
`timeout-minutes` goes from 25 to 35 for a related reason: the budget is checked
between cells, so a process that starts the most expensive cell just under the
line runs about 690 s past it. 1020 + 690 + setup is a little under 30 minutes.
The first wave of sectors 0-11 says the sizing is right. Six shards, 1160 of
1160 cells done inside the budget, none refused, 0.053 to 0.102 seconds per box
across runners against the 0.10008 the projection assumed.
This commit runs sectors 12-23, 174 jobs, same target 0.0153040536. It queues
behind the sectors 0-11 run on the workflow's concurrency group.

* Hunt #80 section 5: sweep the cells the two runs left, and buy the exact count
Two runs of the away branch at target 0.0153040536 leave a small remainder: a
shard whose processes hit their wall budget stops between cells, which is the
design working, and the cells it did not reach are simply still open. Sectors
0-11 left 345 of 19,200, or 1.8 percent, and every one of the nine jobs the
25-minute timeout cancelled still uploaded the cells it had reached.
This run does three things.
It sweeps. `mode: sweep` re-plans all 24 sectors at a much coarser shard size
and hands each shard a skip list, so a shard does only the cells still missing
and most of them do nothing at all.
It builds that skip list ONCE, in the plan job, and publishes it as a single
artifact. Having each of 121 shards download both prior runs' 340 artifacts
would have been forty thousand API calls against a thousand-per-hour token,
which is a rate-limit failure dressed up as a flaky run. The list is compacted
to the four fields the worker reads and lands in `skip/`, deliberately not in
`out/`, because `out/*` is what a shard uploads and what the roll-up reads back.
It buys the exact-count oracle. Sectors 0 and 1 are additionally run at the
published target 0.0153, where the archive's reference logs give terminal-box
counts of 270,744 and 292,931 to match exactly. At the raised target the counts
must come out slightly above the reference, which is a consistency check and not
an equality, so the equality has to be bought somewhere and this is where.
Two things that fall out of running one sector at two targets, both fixed here
before they could produce a wrong number rather than after:
`ci_plan.py collect` de-duplicates on (sector, cell), so without a target
filter a cell's record at one target would silently stand in for its record at
the other, and the per-sector box count, which is the entire cross-check,
would be a mixture of two runs.
`--skip-done` matched on the sector alone, so an oracle shard would have
skipped cells already accepted at the raised target. Both now match the
target, and both are checked: at 0.0153 against a 0.0153040536 skip list the
worker reports cells_to_do 4, skipped_done 0, where the same call at the
matching target reports 1 and 3.

* Hunt #80 section 5: the verifier accepts a higher target, and the doors
Wikstrom's own verifier, unmodified, on his own unmodified certificate data,
accepts sqrt(3)/4 + 0.0153040536. He published 0.0153. Every one of the 24 away
sectors, all 38,400 initial cells, zero cells refused anywhere.
That target is also the end of the road for that data. The near branch's Arb
gain is 0.0153040536989472, a rigorous lower bound (verify_near_moment returns
float_lower of its ball), and the dichotomy's gain is min(near, away), so it is
the supremum of what the shipped certificate supports without regenerating a
stored number. The published constant was leaving 4.05e-6 of its own certificate
unclaimed. Section 2a said the away branch was not what pinned the run; that is
now shown rather than inferred, with 3.4e-4 still to spare.
This is a statement about the finite certificate and not about Bloch's constant.
The step from an accepted target to B is Bonk's theorem, the moment inequality,
the three-atom reduction and the centre-placement lemma, and this hunt audits
none of them.
The run's own cross-check is exact. Sectors 0 and 1 were additionally rerun at
the PUBLISHED target, where reference-run/logs records a terminal-box count to
match, and both match to the integer: 270,744 and 292,931, assembled from 3,200
independent branch_verify calls on a machine the author never used. Sector 0 is
the better of the two, because its archived log is not a fresh run at all but a
checkpoint resume recording zero boxes of work. At the raised target the counts
land 0.87% above the archive's, every sector between +0.58% and +1.25%, which is
the price of the raise and not a discrepancy.
Cost, measured: 476 jobs across five workflow runs, 114.8 runner-hours of
GitHub-hosted machine time billed zero, 324.1 core-hours of Arb subdivision, 9.1
hours of wall clock. The estimate published in RUNS.md before anything launched
said 321 core-hours; the run spent 307.4 at the raised target, 4.2% under. Nine
jobs were cancelled by their own timeout and every one still uploaded the cells
it had reached, so they cost nine partial shards rather than nine shards. The
attempt this replaces lost a whole shard on every preemption, which is why six
hours of it produced nothing.
Section 1's SECTORS-PLACEHOLDER is filled in the same pass: two of the archive's
24 away-sector counts are now reproduced exactly and the other 22 stay REPORTED.
The hunt now ends with a doors section, per the ceiling-hunt doctrine: the five
active constraints ranked with the slope measured for each, the ten-row
frozen-constant inventory with the trade shape of each, and the information
class. The top door is regenerating the certificate data at moved ETA, LARGE_RAD
and node count, which section 4 puts at ~0.015359. It is affordable: the away
side of a 0.015316 target costs 4.2% more boxes than 0.0153, against the 1.0%
this run paid. What stops it is a prepare-and-publish step the instrument does
not have, not compute.
Nothing was posted to the author, to Zenodo or to arXiv.

36c607038f0c5d0c836fca1376bdc3879eec4b4b.subject: Hunt #78: trust map for the seven-point simple-zero bound (#98)
36c607038f0c5d0c836fca1376bdc3879eec4b4b.body: * Hunt #78: trust map for the seven-point simple-zero bound
files: Grades every step from F6 >= c to the asymptotic proportion as
LEAN-BACKED / ARB-ENCLOSED / HANDWRITTEN / MISSING, and recovers the
map from the finite constant to the published bound in closed form.
The map: Phi(c,m,p) = (H - 6(m-1)/(pm)) / (1 - c(m-6)/m), reproducing
both published constants to 40 digits. The block size m is not free:
A_0 = c(m-6) <= 1 (riemann.tex:375, forced by the min{1,...} in the
block-defect lemma at :354) caps it at 6 + floor(1/c), and both
published values sit exactly at their cap. That is why raising the
target lowered m from 269 to 267, and it makes the bound sawtoothed in
c rather than monotone. The family's apparent ceiling at p = 3000 is
0.673025477, 4.1e-6 above the Gohms claim and 5.6% of the room under
the configuration ceiling.
Verdict B, one substantial analytic bridge. Six of sixteen steps are
already kernel-checked in anthropics/zeta-23-lean, including Theorem D
itself, von Neumann, and the Hermitian positive-part splitting; four
more are small finite statements. What is missing is carrying the new
spectral defect term through the tail passage and establishing the
limiting overlap kernel uniformly in T. Smallest obligation, stated in
Lean-takeable form: the stability rank-trace lemma, a strict
strengthening of RankTrace.lean:163 whose every ingredient is already a
named declaration in the same namespace.
Two defects recorded. The Gohms variant changes only the target and
leaves PRESSURE_CUTOFF_CELLS at 45600, so its outer-region prune proves
only 19/5000 on the 3087 boxes it discards; the claim is probably true
and that run does not establish it. And the lab has been quoting the
configuration ceiling as 0.68185, a decimal appearing once in a remark
with no proof attached, where the Lean development proves
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* TRUST-MAP: record the EnclOK hypothesis and the undistributed certificate behind the Lean ceiling
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* TRUST-MAP: the gated pressure sweep, and the S9 status stated precisely
The pressure-denominator question is answered rather than left open. Three
global-search strategies failed their own gate at p=3000 (floors 0.003868 to
0.004140 against the known 0.0038262312114228695) because the true minimiser
is not palindromic and sums to 9.085 while every basin they found was
symmetric and summed near 10.08. Exhaustive seeding from the first four
positive zeros of k, 4^6 = 4096 starts, recovers the floor and the argmin to
1.2e-13, so it gates the table.
Result: the curve is unimodal with its peak near p = 3200, and the published
3000 is very nearly at it. Retuning is worth 2.24e-6, taking the family's
apparent ceiling to 0.673027719, which is 6.36e-6 above the Gohms claim and
5.64% of the room under the configuration ceiling. A mild negative result:
the third leg is nearly exhausted already.
Also states S9's status precisely instead of calling it absent. zeta-23-lean
has the Poisson identity, the finite-L transform PhiR, the Montgomery-Taylor
profile vStar, and a closed-form cosine-window autocorrelation; what it lacks
is k = K/K(0), the L -> oo limit, and above all the uniformity in T that is
the actual content.

a9c482f72c81d84dab740c11531b4409be928706.subject: Hunt #79: Ainta's S2 is an instance of an upstream theorem (Aristotle probe, no submission) (#102)
a9c482f72c81d84dab740c11531b4409be928706.body: * Hunt #79: Ainta's S2 is an instance of an upstream theorem
files: The formal-native Aristotle probe on the stability rank-trace lemma. The
theorem is proved and builds with zero sorrys, and no Aristotle project was
opened, because after the local pass nothing remained to send.
Two findings, neither of them the proof.
S2 is not new relative to the Lean development the trust map chose as its
vocabulary. Ainta's profile Psi is that development's own gc 2 shifted by one,
Psi = gc 2 + 1, the shift being exactly Psi 0 = 1, which is the bookkeeping that
trades a rank count for Fintype.card r. The sharpened scalar estimate the trust
map expected to need is already sq_sub_ge_gc; the V Vᴴ / VᴴV spectral transfer
is already sum_eigenvalues_comm; and the theorem falls out as a corollary of
Zeta23.ZeroSide.RankTraceMult.rank_trace_mult at c = 2, evaluated at the
eigenbasis presentation of V Vᴴ. The map searched Zeta23/LinAlg/ (the paper's
section 3) and not Zeta23/ZeroSide/ (what upstream flags as beyond Theorems
A-E). Two things the formal state exposed that the transcription hides: the
rank hypothesis is removable, so a sharp form holds with no hypothesis on V at
all, and hV is load-bearing for exactly one inequality, tr(V Vᴴ) <= card r.
Second: hunts/frontier_math/zeta23ext does not assemble on main at 36c6070.
assemble.sh reports three failing targets, RetentionWired, EForm2.Bridge and
TruncEst.Kernel, with Retention.margin_identity picking up sorryAx as a
consequence. Not the dependency store, not the Zeta23 dependency, not this
branch. Recorded as issue #101; not fixed here. The new module builds standalone
and no claim is made that the package assembles.
New: Zeta23Ext/StableRankTrace.lean, eleven declarations, eleven #print axioms
lines in the module so the audit reruns on every build, all reporting
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Non-vacuity run in both directions: the
Psi := 0 shadow is proved independently from rank_trace_ineq_two, and is also
implied by the theorem via Psi_nonneg.
check_stable_rank_trace.py measures what the kernel does not: the sharp form is
an equality on the family upstream proves extremal for Lemma R (400 instances,
slack 1.07e-14, float grade), and the trust map's form discards a mean of 6.05
on random draws.
Palomar: both existing surfaces still pass the mechanical precheck (64/0/1 and
57/0/1). A third entry is not recommended and was not authored; a bridging
corollary of an existing public Lean theorem does not clear that registry's
notability floor.
S2 is one step of sixteen. S8 and S9 are untouched, the seven-point theorem is
not verified, and nothing here bears on RH.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
* Probe write-up: correct upstream line refs, sharpen the card-r accounting
`sum_eigenvalues_comm` is RankTraceMult.lean:189 and `rank_trace_mult` is :281,
not :190 and :280. And section 2 said Ainta's card-r bookkeeping and [L23]'s
rank bookkeeping were "the same accounting", which is loose: the identity is
that the Psi 0 = 1 shift and the rank-to-card-r switch cancel term for term,
leaving the defect S on top of [L23]'s UNRELAXED -rho. Stated that way.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
* Drop an unpinned claim from a docstring
stable_rank_trace_sharp's docstring asserted the defect is >= -card r. That is
true but needs an argument nothing here proves (gc 2 >= -1 pointwise bounds the
sum by -card n; getting to -card r uses gc 2 0 = 0 and rank P <= card r). House
rule is that a claim in a docstring is pinned or hedged, so it is replaced by the
identity rtrace_specMap_Psi actually proves.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
* Correct an unfair claim about the trust map, and state the real gap
An earlier draft said the trust map "did not look in Zeta23/ZeroSide/". That is
false. TRUST-MAP.md:382 already cites RankTraceMult.lean:281, TightMult.lean:93
(lemmaR_tight) and gc by its definition, and it tells a formalizer to read
lemmaR_tight first. Publishing the original claim would have been an unfair
criticism of a sibling hunt's work.
The real gap is one step further in and is more useful. The map filed upstream's
defect as "a different one", spectral versus per-zero. But rank_trace_mult is
universally quantified over presentations P = Pmat m v, and at the eigenbasis
presentation its per-zero defect IS the spectral defect; upstream's own
sum_gc_eigenvalues_ge is that comparison in one direction, with the eigenbasis as
the equality case. And Psi was never matched to gc 2, so section 4 pointed the
proof at RankTrace.lean:52-56 for a scalar estimate that RankTraceMult.lean:81
already proves. Two sections of the same map hold the two halves and never meet.
The transferable rule changes accordingly: not "search harder", which the map did
fine, but "when a formalization already carries an object of the right shape,
check whether the target is an instance of it before recording it as different".
The mechanical test is to write both profiles as one-variable functions and
subtract.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
* Attribute the contrast paragraph to the right trust-map section
TRUST-MAP.md:382 is in section 2 (the step table), not section 5. The point is
unchanged: the step table records RankTraceMult as a contrast and section 4 then
states the obligation as if it did not apply.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
* Section 10: name what formalization actually bought here
The pilot's sharpest result is not that Lean proved the lemma, it is that a prose
map had gc's definition in front of it and recorded it as a different object. In
prose, "a per-zero term gc c x = x^2 - cx - ((x-c)+)^2" and "Psi t = (t-1)^2 for
t <= 2, 2t - 3 beyond" read as two things. Having to write one real function that
specMap accepts turns them into two expressions of one type, and subtracting is
then the obvious move.
So what formalization bought was not rigour, which the prose map already had. It
was an enforced normal form in which two descriptions of the same object cannot
stay different-looking. That belongs in the answer to the only question the pilot
was built to answer.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
* Palomar section: name the mechanical blocker, not just the notability one
A Palomar replay builds the submission project from a fixed commit. If that
project is hunts/frontier_math/zeta23ext, the replay builds a project that does
not build today (section 1b, issue #101). So a third surface is blocked on #101
regardless of the notability judgement, and #101 is three unrelated modules of
port work.
Kept apart from the theorem's status on purpose: the module builds standalone and
the three failures are elsewhere in the package, so this is a packaging blocker
and not a reason to doubt the result.

c1f79aca007ddc849cea6674324ea4d5bcbda8c3.subject: Hunt #79: what it would take to prove the certificate itself (#117)
c1f79aca007ddc849cea6674324ea4d5bcbda8c3.body: The Lean bridge proves the n-point simple-zero bound conditional on the finite
files: inequality hCert, at every n. This is the feasibility study of proving hCert
itself, plus the first slice of it proved.
Ranked route: (b), the verified-checker route. Route (a), interval arithmetic
by tactic, is dead on the range-minimum queries alone: box_lower makes 21 of
them per node, the widest surviving gap component spans 34 256 cells, and a
tactic proof would re-establish each minimum at each of 707 901 nodes, about 59
CPU-days for the queries before any proof term is written. (b) at least has a
design, and it decomposes into eight obligations, two of which are now proved.
The slice, in hunts/ainta_seven_point/lean/, a Lake package that requires
lean/bridge BY PATH, so every theorem in it is about the same Kfun, kfun, wfun,
F, F6 that seven_point_bound_lab uses. Nothing is transcribed and there is no
restatement to audit. lake build CertRoute: 8842 jobs, zero errors, zero sorry,
zero axiom, zero native_decide, and all eleven audited declarations report
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
certGoal / certGoal_eq_hypothesis
the obligation stated exactly, and Iff.rfl that it IS the hypothesis
Zeta23Ext.Bridge.seven_point_bound_lab consumes.
Kfun_eq_sinc
the integral that defines the kernel equals the sinc form the Arb
verifier evaluates, at every real x including the two removable
singularities. Defs.lean asserted this in a docstring; the string "sinc"
occurs exactly once in lean/bridge/Zeta23Ext/, in that docstring. Every
route needs it, because no interval arithmetic runs on an integral.
cos_sin_taylor12
a twelve-term Taylor enclosure of sin and cos on [-1,1] from
Complex.exp_bound, error 13/(12! * 12) = 2.26e-9. Mathlib at the pinned
revision has no numerical evaluator for sin or cos and no
interval-arithmetic tactic; its sharpest bound is Real.cos_bound at
5/96 * theta^4, about 2e-2 at theta = 0.79, and a kernel table needs 1e-9.
kfun_closed / gam_bounds
k(x) = (cos b - 2*gam*b*sin b)/(1 - 2b^2) with b = pi*x and one
transcendental constant gam = (1/sqrt 2)cot(1/sqrt 2) = 3/2 - H, enclosed
to 1e-6. One constant per table rather than two sinc values per cell, and
the argument reduction is exact in x because the period is exactly 2.
wfun_cell_4160_lower
the pivotal artifact: w >= 23/100000 on the closed cell
x in [1.04, 1.04025], cell 4160 of the verifier's 1/4000 grid, inside the
first surviving gap component so a cell the search actually queries. An
exact-rational interval evaluation of the same closed form gives 2.3164e-4
and the true minimum is 2.3171e-4, so the kernel-checked bound is 99.3% of
what the arithmetic allows.
Measured, on this machine.
One cell lemma, by deletion (one copy of the theorem versus six, touch before
each run, two runs of each): 6.37 s and 5.68 s against 14.51 s and 13.39 s,
so 1.63 s and 1.54 s marginal per cell. Take 1.6 s.
The table bill: 47 196 kernel cells and 43 396 second-derivative cells at the
advertised parameters (7, 34697/10^7, 3400), 90 592 cell lemmas, 40.3
CPU-hours flat, about 160 after three upward corrections that are stated and
not measured. Large, parallel, and not what stops the project.
Kernel reduction, decide on a balanced binary traversal (2^d leaves, depth d,
five Nat operations per node, the shape a branch-and-bound checker has, since
the real tree has maximum depth 37):
2 047 nodes     122 ms      60 us/node
32 767 nodes    2545 ms      78 us/node
131 071 nodes   11063 ms      84 us/node
524 287 nodes   did not finish in 11 minutes of CPU, 2.1 GB resident
Linear at 84 us per five-operation node to 1.3e5 nodes, then a cliff. The real
search is 707 901 nodes at p = 3000 and 1 112 733 at p = 3400, each node at
least thirty times heavier. native_decide would remove this and is refused by
lean/proof_adapter.py on this repository's own rule.
So the wall is the search, not the table, which is the opposite of what the
sizes suggest, and the seven-point instance is not viable at present.
The instance that is: n = 3. The same parametric n_point_bound at
at 50 digits, which is 2.42e-4 ABOVE the unconditional H = 0.67250070367941164573
that the dependency proves. Its search is 342 nodes, six thousand times inside
the measured envelope, and its table is 29 488 cell lemmas rather than 90 592.
Discharging hCert there would make an improvement on Theorem D unconditional and
kernel-checked. That is the recommendation, and it is a smaller number than
0.673029553 and a different kind of number.
Not done, and section 6 of the note says so at length: no checker, not even a
toy one, and no soundness lemma for one; no w'' cell bound, which is 43 396 of
the 90 592 lemmas and the harder half; no general cell, the one proved has its
reduced argument already inside [-1,1]; no test of whether the search terminates
without the tangent prune, which fires on 13.2% of nodes; no measurement of a
range-minimum lookup in the kernel under any encoding, which is the largest
unmeasured quantity in the search projection; no empirical attempt at route (a).
lean/bridge is untouched. The Palomar submission surface, both comparator files
and both formalization files are byte-identical, and the new package requires
the bridge rather than joining it. Nothing here contradicts RESULTS.md,
TRUST-MAP.md or BRIDGE.md: the certificate remains an interval-arithmetic
verifier's acceptance and not a Lean fact, at every n, and formalization.yaml's
line that re-enclosing the table inside Lean is "a separate project of a
different size" stands. This is the size.

files: The Lean side of discharging n_point_bound's hCert hypothesis at n = 3.
hunts/ainta_seven_point/lean-three-point/ is a Lake package that requires
lean/bridge BY PATH, so every theorem in it is about the same Kfun, kfun, wfun,
F and Phi_n that Zeta23Ext.Bridge.n_point_bound consumes. Nothing in lean/bridge

Architecture: w >= 0 gives a pressure cutoff at g0 + g1 >= c*p, so only the
triangle needs cells; a one-dimensional cover confines the two-dimensional work
to four near-zero intervals; a single general cell lemma (wfun_ge) applied many
times, with the Taylor enclosure from #117 reproduced in ThreePoint/Base.lean.
Not yet built anywhere. The workflow that builds it, and THREE-POINT.md with its

* Hunt #79: the three-point certificate written in Lean, and the CI that cannot start
Three things land here and one does not.
Lands: a fixed generator, a pre-flight validator, and the write-up.
three_point_gen.py had a real bug. cover1 emitted `Or.inr Or.inr (Or.inl e)`,
which is Or.inr applied to two explicit arguments rather than nesting: a type
error in three places that would have failed the first build. Fixed at the
emit site, not in the output. Two tactic chains were also hardened before
spending a build on them (F3_eq's trailing `ring` -> `try ring`; Phi_three's
norm_num/field_simp chain -> push_cast + div_eq_div_iff + ring).
three_point_preflight.py asks the question the Lean kernel is not available to
answer: is the certificate arithmetically true? It checks all 368 cell
constants against a 401-point sweep of the true w, checks that cover1's chain
is contiguous over [0, 4.035] and that every table cell clears c, and replays
all 487 leaves of the four box trees to confirm the cells invoked really cover
the x, y and x+y ranges the branch conditions force and that each linarith is
actually true. Exit 0, zero problems, 3 seconds. It is a filter, not a proof,
and it is not in the trust chain.
THREE-POINT.md is the write-up, with c re-chosen from a re-measured
cost-vs-c table at thirteen values. c = 1345/10^6, m = 745, p = 3000,
H + 2.3663e-4. It also corrects the brief: c = 1353/10^6 is not out of reach
of the enclosure, only of the proof size (4127 cells, 59361 leaves).
Does not land: the workflow. It is written and parked at ci/three-point.yml
because the token this branch was pushed with lacks the `workflow` scope, and
git push, the contents API and the git-data API all refuse to place a file under
.github/workflows/ without it. Granting an OAuth scope is the operator's call,
so the file carries the two commands that move it into place.
Consequence, stated plainly in the note: NOTHING HERE IS A THEOREM YET. The
development is sorry-free and native_decide-free by inspection and its
arithmetic is checked, but no kernel has seen it and there is no axiom audit to
report.

The cache carries the toolchain itself; installing elan first and restoring over
it is the wrong order. full.yml's lean job restores first and that is the shape
to copy. Validated as YAML: 20 steps, timeout-minutes 350, triggers push on this

Counted directly: 1515 occurrences of wc_N in Main.lean, of which 22 are in
