* Hunt #79: the first build, and the three things it found
Run 32683784986. Mathlib olean cache 1m25s, dependencies 11m24s, ThreePoint.Base
26s, the seven cell tables 5m33s + 5m36s + ... , all success. 368 cell lemmas and
473 lines of enclosure machinery elaborate, including everything that had never
been elaborated before: wfun_ge, sinc_taylor, wfun_window across the removable
singularity, the nine cs_* anchors, and gam_bounds tightened to 1.11e-8.
ThreePoint.Main failed, on three mechanical faults and nothing mathematical.
le_or_lt does not exist at this Mathlib pin. Replaced by le_total, which is
bedrock and gives closed-on-both-sides branches -- which is exactly what
three_point_preflight.py already modelled, so its 487-leaf validation carries
over unchanged and still passes.
HD, Ncount and N0simple were unresolved. They live in Zeta23.ThmD and
Zeta23.ZeroSide, and eventually_atTop in Filter; the module opened only Real,
which it never used. Now it opens exactly what lean/bridge's own Main.lean
opens. With autoImplicit on, each unresolved name had been silently auto-bound
into a variable, so the advertised statements were statements about nothing.
That is worth its own hardening pass and is NOT done here.
The axiom-audit step in the workflow would have false-failed on a clean audit:
the pattern was anchored ^\S+ but Lake prefixes every diagnostic with
info: <file>:<line>:<col>:. Re-anchored on the tail of the axiom list, and the
trailing $ dropped so a carriage return cannot trip it.
Phi_three is already confirmed correct by the failure itself: ring reduced both
sides to -9225608246/93125 + <atom> * 148800133, matching the constant computed
by hand, and failed only because HD was garbage. The cross-multiplication chain
is right.
Base and the seven cell tables are byte-identical, so the rolling cache key means
this round rebuilds Main alone.
* Hunt #79: give the box lemmas a heartbeat budget that fits the binding basin
Run 32686863542: every name error is gone and the cache did its job -- 4m29s
total, dependencies and Base and all seven cell tables restored, only Main
rebuilt. One failure left, and it is a resource limit rather than mathematics:
ThreePoint/Main.lean:204: (deterministic) timeout at tactic execution,
maximum number of heartbeats (200000) has been reached
A box lemma is a single declaration holding its whole bisection tree, so the
tree shares one heartbeat budget. pair_0_1 is B1 x B2, which carries 453 of the
487 leaves because the binding basin is at (1.0508, 2.0025), and it ran out
about 4% of the way in after 43 s. Scaled, it wants roughly 5 million; the
budget is set to 10 million for headroom.
This is a compile-resource knob and nothing else. It is not an axiom, it does
not appear in #print axioms, and it is emitted on the four generated box lemmas
only -- never on three_point_cert, Phi_three, three_point_bound or
three_point_bound_ratio, which carry the default.
The structural fix is to split pair_0_1 so each subtree gets its own budget and
they compile in parallel. Not done: measure first, then decide whether the
wall clock justifies the generator work.
* Hunt #79: fix the doc-comment order, and hand the leaf steps their cell lemma directly
Run 32687291025 is the informative one. It produced exactly four errors, all of
them mine, all of them parse errors:
ThreePoint/Main.lean:99:54: unexpected token 'set_option'; expected 'lemma'
I emitted `set_option ... in` AFTER the doc comment, and a doc comment must
attach directly to a declaration. Lean recovered past each one and parsed the
`set_option ... in lemma` that followed as its own command, so the ENTIRE
development elaborated: no heartbeat timeout, no unknown constants, Main in
16m23s. The raised budget works and the four orphaned doc comments are all that
stood between this and a green build.
Two changes.
The set_option now precedes the doc comment. Confirmed on AXLE in 0.9 s --
doc-then-option okay=False, option-then-doc okay=True -- which is the check
that should have preceded the 19-minute round it cost.
1393 of the 1443 leaf steps asked for a constant that IS the cell lemma's own
constant, and wrote `le_trans (by norm_num) (wc_k x _ _)` to get it. That
makes the elaborator postpone a `by norm_num` against a metavariable until the
second argument fixes it, for a proof of `W <= W`. They now apply the cell
lemma directly. le_trans in Main drops from 1515 to 125, the survivors being
cover1's 22 (where the constant really is weaker) and the 50 straddle blocks
(where it is a minimum of two).
MEASURED on AXLE, 500 leaf steps of each shape, Mathlib only: the direct form
is 1.11x faster, 5.2 ms per step, about 7 s across the package. Real but
small -- so the honest finding is that the le_trans idiom is NOT what
exhausted the heartbeat budget. The leaf count in a single declaration is.
three_point_preflight.py was taught the new leaf form and still reports 368 cell
lemmas, 487 leaves, 0 problems.
* Hunt #79: the certificate is proved; fix the audit that misread its own success
Run 32688543779: ThreePoint.Main SUCCESS, the whole library SUCCESS. All six
advertised declarations report
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
and nothing else. three_point_cert is proved, and three_point_bound is an
unconditional theorem at Phi_3 = (149000000 * HD 1 - 99200)/148800133.
The job still went red, on my own audit step rather than on Lean. `lake build`
replays the diagnostics of every cached module, so main-build.log carries the
whole dependency tree's #print axioms output; the bridge prints
[propext, choice, Quot.sound] wherever Classical is open, which is the same
three axioms under a shorter name, and a blanket pattern reads it as a
violation. The audit now scopes itself to Zeta23Ext.Bridge.ThreePoint.*, accepts
`choice` and `Classical.choice` as the one axiom they are, and requires all six
advertised names to be found -- so a build that printed nothing cannot audit
clean. Tested against three fixtures: the real run-4 log passes, a planted
sorryAx on three_point_cert fails, an empty log fails.
MEASURED, the leaf-shape change from the previous commit, at package scale:
ThreePoint.Main 16m23s -> 14m49s, a 9.6% reduction. AXLE's controlled 500-step
test attributes about 7 s of that to dropping le_trans; the rest is either the
1390 lines the file lost or run-to-run variance, and n=1 per shape does not
separate them. Said that way in THREE-POINT.md rather than claimed as a 9.6%
win for the idiom.
* Hunt #79: the write-up, rewritten around a green build
Run 32689888754 is green end to end. THREE-POINT.md is no longer a note about a
proof script nobody had compiled; it is the note about a theorem, and it keeps
the failures rather than tidying them away, because four of the five runs failed
and four of those failures were mine.
What changed in the note:
The header states the result and prints the axiom audit. Section 1 stops
hedging with "if the build closes". Section 5 is now The build rather than
The blocker: the per-module cold cost, the five-run table with what each run
bought, the one set_option and what it is not, and the audit that took two

Section 4's pre-flight provenance is kept but reframed. It predicted risk in
the wrong place: all 25 never-elaborated declarations compiled first time, and
the failures came from identifier renames and a heartbeat budget instead.
The cost guess is replaced by the measurement, and it was half wrong. The
guess was that nlinarith on long rational literals dominates. The seven cell

the build, because 453 of its 487 leaves sit in one declaration. Structure
mattered as much as tactic choice.
Section 7 gains the two things not done and names them plainly: pair_0_1 is
not split, and autoImplicit is still on. The second is the sharpest thing the
loop found -- it is what let four unresolved identifiers become variables and
the advertised statements become statements about nothing -- and it should be

RUNS.md carries the run manifest. Contribution contract PASS, CONTEXT.md
up to date, no regeneration required.
* Turn autoImplicit off, so an unresolved name cannot pass as a theorem
The first build of this package stated its advertised theorems about free
variables named HD, Ncount and N0simple rather than the bridge's definitions,
because autoImplicit silently binds an unresolved identifier instead of
reporting it. It errored only because a variable cannot be applied to an
argument; had those names been nullary the file would have compiled and the
theorems would have said nothing while looking exactly like success.
The green build is not affected — those names resolve, which is why they take

dbabd518209c045e74444bcb51d1aadbe17e086d.subject: Palomar surface for the unconditional three-point theorem (#130)
dbabd518209c045e74444bcb51d1aadbe17e086d.body: V2 of the bridge entry. It replaces V1's four seven-point statements with the
files: parametric n-point theorem and two instances: the eight-point one, still
conditional on its certificate at the leading constant, and the three-point
one, which carries no hypothesis at all.
`three_point_bound` and `three_point_bound_ratio` are the point of it. Their
certificate is `Zeta23Ext.Bridge.ThreePoint.three_point_cert`, proved in Lean
from a twelve-term Taylor enclosure of `cos` and `sin`, the closed form of `K`,
and 368 interval cell lemmas applied 1515 times over 487 leaves. The constant
dependency's unconditional `H = 0.67250070367941164` by 2.3663e-4, so for
Mathlib's `riemannZeta` this is an unconditional improvement of that
development's Theorem D, under the three standard axioms and no hypothesis.
Layout. The `ThreePoint` modules move out of their own Lake package and become a
second `lean_lib` of `lean/bridge`. The old package required `lean/bridge` by a
relative path pointing outside itself, and whether the registry's replay
resolves such a dependency is not something this repository can determine; the
project directory is now the one the live entry already replays, whose
dependency set the move leaves untouched. `autoImplicit` stays off, for that
library alone, through `leanOptions` on its `lean_lib`.
`BridgeChallenge.lean`, `BridgeSolution.lean`, `comparator.json` and
`formalization.yaml` are byte-identical: V1 is live at 58bd44ca and nothing
about it moved. The staged eight-point files are renamed to V2 because the
format allows one Challenge module and one Solution module per comparator, and
a module advertising both instances cannot honestly be called "Eight".
Origin derives `source-based` under the rules in `scripts/palomar_precheck.py`,
not `original`: the Ainta paper is related as `adapts`. Precheck is 63 pass,
1 warn (the rc toolchain, standing), 0 FAIL. AXLE reports zero errors on the
Challenge and exactly five `sorry` warnings, one per advertised statement.

01f675121d3925f084058cb2e82159a02bc64006.subject: The four-point certificate, proved in Lean: an unconditional 0.6728470198 (#135)
01f675121d3925f084058cb2e82159a02bc64006.body: * Four-point certificate: generator, tree and CI
files: `hunts/ainta_seven_point/lean-four-point/` discharges `n_point_bound`'s
certificate hypothesis at `n = 4`, `c = 2310/10^6`, `p = 2500`, for an
against the proved three-point `0.6727373345` and `H = 0.6725007037`.
Not built yet: this commit exists to start the CI loop.
Structure, one dimension up from `three_point_gen.py` and the same
architecture: one general cell lemma applied many times, a 1-D cover, a
bisection tree. Three things are new and each is forced by `F 4`:
* the adjacent-pair coefficient is `2/3`, so the 1-D cover runs at level
`3c/2`, not at `c` -- a cleared gap has to pay for the whole `c` on its
own through a coefficient smaller than one;
* the region is a tetrahedron, so the boxes are triples and the bisection
is three-dimensional;
* the tree is cut into 76 chunk lemmas of at most 110 leaves each,
bin-packed across 16 modules, so that no declaration holds thousands of
leaves on one heartbeat budget and one core.
983 cell lemmas, 3315 leaves, 13 boxes, 44 of the 64 dispatch cases dead
by the pressure cutoff.
Validated before pushing: `four_point_preflight.py` reads the generated
Lean (not the generator's tree) and checks every cell against a 401-point
sweep, the cover's contiguity, all 3315 leaf inequalities, all 76 router
regions and all 64 dispatch cases -- 0 problems, and it was fault-injected
four ways to confirm it can fail. The three new anchor lemmas, `F4_eq`,
`Phi_four`, the transpose rewrite and the `((2500:N):R)` bridge in the
advertised wrapper were each settled on a Mathlib-only fragment in about
a second rather than a CI round.
* The four-point certificate is proved: FOUR-POINT.md and the run record
Run 32738666418 is green end to end on the FIRST build, no iteration, and all
six advertised declarations report [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and
nothing else.
Phi_4 - H  = 3.4632e-04  =  1.464x the three-point gain
`four_point_bound` has no hypotheses, zero sorry, zero native_decide.
Measured cost: Mathlib cache 1m36s, dependencies 11m00s, Base 26s, the 17 cell
modules 1h46m43s, Cover 27s, the 16 chunk modules 1h13m48s, Boxes 1m36s, Main
20s. Whole job 3h18m30s. That is 6.51 s per cell lemma and 1.34 s per leaf.
Three things the build settled that the projection got wrong, all in
FOUR-POINT.md §5:
* lake did not spread the modules over four cores, so un-staging the build
bought nothing and every projected time was ~3x optimistic. Both routes were
divided by the same wrong number, so the ranking held.
* chunking is worth what THREE-POINT.md §7 guessed and left undone: 1.34 s per
leaf against 1.83 s for leaves carrying HALF the work, and FourPoint.Main
costs 20 seconds against the three-point Main's 14m49s.
* a GitHub Actions cache cannot be read across branches, so the three-point
restore-key matched nothing in 0s.
How much further it goes, measured rather than guessed (§6): c = 2325/10^6 fits
inside the workflow's 350-minute cap with forty minutes of margin and
c = 2330/10^6 needs 431 minutes and does not. But the soft wall bites first --
the next rung returns 1.6e-6 of constant per CI-hour against the 3.32e-5 this
run returned, which is twenty times worse than the run just made and three times
worse than route (b), the route rejected on exactly that ground. So the
deliverable stays at c = 2310/10^6, and §6 is the measurement that says why.
* Correct the gap-closing figure in FOUR-POINT.md
The draft said Phi_4 closes 21% of the gap between the proved Phi_3 and the
conditional seven-point value. Recomputed: Phi_3 stood 44.7% of the way from H
to 0.673029553, Phi_4 stands 65.5%, so Phi_4 closes 37.5% of what was still open
after Phi_3. Against the eight-point 0.673052982 the figure is 62.7%.
No other number in the note moves; this one was never derived, only asserted.

9918818bf69309700b451da71b6bfec6898be118.subject: Palomar v2: cite the competing constants, and correct two decimal tails (#152)
9918818bf69309700b451da71b6bfec6898be118.body: The v1 review registered with one non-blocking warning: the literature
files: account omitted competing public work already documented in this
repository, so a reader could not tell how the advertised unconditional
constants relate to the published field.
Cited, with the distinction stated rather than implied:
- Gohms, issue #1 on ainta/zeta-simple-zeros, 191/50000 at m = 267 and
p = 3000, giving 0.6730213619501665... Added as a `web discussion`
source, relationship `background`. Nothing here depends on it.
- Ainta's own constant 0.6730085279277797613... written into its source
note with its parameters.
- Both exceed the two unconditional instances advertised here. Both rest
on an interval-arithmetic program accepting a finite inequality and on
an informal passage from that inequality to a proportion of zeros;
neither step is a theorem about riemannZeta. That is the distinction,
and it is now in the abstract, the source notes and the project README.
- The reproduction of both runs at 040c5e8, the compactification-prune
defect, and the re-run under a target-derived cutoff (every published
claim survived) are recorded, with the public report of 2026-08-23.
- `author_endorsement` for both moved to `no-response`: they were
contacted, in public, on that issue.
Separately, and found while checking the table: the printed decimal
expansions of the two unconditional constants were wrong in their tails.
The Lean statements use the exact closed forms
and are untouched, as are the parameters (m = 745, m = 435) and the
quoted improvement 2.3663e-4. Both closed forms reproduce to 30 digits
at 120-dps; the printed tails did not, diverging at the 18th and 16th
decimal, which is where float64 runs out. The correction is to comments
and metadata only. Verified against Ainta's published constant, which
this same computation reproduces to all 20 quoted digits.
hunts/ainta_seven_point/RUNS.md still carries the old tails in two run
records and is deliberately left alone: it is a dated log, not an

5d5f27f21be9f51abf20a77894acf200b2ec89fb.subject: ainta_seven_point: rescue verify_n.py into the record, and fault-inject it
5d5f27f21be9f51abf20a77894acf200b2ec89fb.body: The n-point verifier behind the eight-point certificate was in no commit of this
files: repository. RESULTS.md said it lived in the upstream clone; that clone is
gitignored, and the file survived in one session's temporary directory. A
referee of the Pub 2 note found the gap by failing to find the file. It is
tracked now (sha256 21af096c...8927) and fetch_upstream.sh installs it into the
pinned clone on every fetch. The true-target control at n = 3 accepts in 342
nodes, the count the 2026-08-23 artifact records, which is the evidence that
this file is the program that produced the record.
verify_n_faults.py is the soundness check the verifier never had. A verifier
cannot be validated by a true instance and node-for-node reproduction is
agreement, not soundness (the published verifier reproduces its own certificate
and is unsound at raised targets). So: a known-false target must be refused,
and four planted unsoundnesses must each flip that refusal. They do, 4 of 4 at
n = 3 and 4 of 4 at n = 7. The first n = 3 attempt was 3 of 4 because
dropped-box removed one of the minimiser's two mirror images; F is
reversal-symmetric, the fault now drops both, and the docstring says why.
Changes no grade. hCert at n = 8 stays a hypothesis; the harness says the
verifier is not broken in four named ways, not that it is a proof assistant.
Closes #159.

2b487026c1ace62b644e305a713e2b3347d05622.body: In steps-per-octave units theta = gamma ln2 / 2pi, Landau's formula is the
files: Fourier coefficient of the zeros mod 1 at frequency log2 n. On Odlyzko's
first 100,000 zeros every prime power n <= 32 lands within 0.0012 of
-Lambda(n)/sqrt(n)/<log(gamma/2pi)> and every composite gives 0.0000; the
smoothed zero density at integer equal temperaments is 0.801 against 0.800
predicted, and the deficit shrinks as 1/log t. The zeros avoid the
temperaments that tune primes and ignore composites. Peak side (Gene Ward
Smith, A117536) reproduced as calibration, with the Riemann-Siegel harmonic
horizon as a caveat. Doc 34, two figures, six tests with a planted fault.

5b4e34b12a7af819912b33b88b896df4065b1461.subject: Hunt #76: correction notice, and the Euler-product discriminator (#91)
5b4e34b12a7af819912b33b88b896df4065b1461.body: The hunt's prior-art account omitted this repository, which had the result.
files: zeta.explicit.prime_spectrum already computes the quantity E1 measures and
its docstring states the identity; on the same 2000 zeros it returns
+392.3556 at u = log 2 where E1 returns -0.09809, the same quantity up to
-2N. A correction notice records that, and a new test pins the duplication
so it cannot be forgotten quietly.
The same review adds what the composite control is actually good for: a
discriminator. For a Dirichlet series with a(1) = 1, the zero spectrum is
the coefficient list of -f'/f, which is supported on prime powers exactly
when f has an Euler product. Measured: zeta 2.8e-31, Davenport-Heilbronn
2.0507 with its loudest single line the composite 51 = 3 x 17, and across
fourteen Epstein discriminants class number one is silent while class
number above one is loud (up to 36.06 at d = -15) and cancels to 1e-30 when
summed over the class group. Nothing here bears on RH: it detects the Euler
product, and DH was already known to lack one.
Also records the process failure in meta/interventions.jsonl.

19bfdae510658cd218f1dd5ca30c1a4db0506010.body: A note-to-hue bijection makes hue distance a function of interval class iff
files: it is affine, so the hue side sees only the choice of a character of Z_12.
Exhaustive search over all 21,772,800 canonical bijections finds the circle
of fifths as the unique argmax of Spearman(hue distance, dissonance) under
three dissonance measures; the perceptual hue circle is not a 12-gon (HSL
adjacent CIEDE2000 steps vary 8.5-fold, twelve equal-tempered steps of light
frequency give hue steps of 1 to 72 degrees). The colour of a chord under
wheel k is its k-th Fourier coefficient, which makes maximal evenness read
as saturation. Doc 33, four figures, 45 tests, CIEDE2000 pinned to Sharma's
34 published pairs.

1b1b99d098f036ba5eee521a0a88ea679d1bab7d.subject: Continue the orbit-18 exact no-good loop and map the Laurent wall
1b1b99d098f036ba5eee521a0a88ea679d1bab7d.body: This commit advances the Krenn-Gu 8x3 support frontier by generating four new orbit-18 support survivors and symmetrically expanding all exact signed-Laurent constraints under the orbit-18 stabilizer.
files: Findings:
1. The orbit-18 stabilizer in S8 x S3 has size 2. Symmetry expansion produced four mirrored cuts, bringing the total loaded constraints to 8.
2. The Laurent sieve hits a systematic algebraic wall. As explicit cuts are added, the minimizer finds supports with progressively fewer zero-binomials.

3. Support #7 (138 entries, 8 cuts loaded) produces an empty signed lattice (0 zero-binomials). The Laurent sieve architecture fails completely on these supports, proving that orbit 18 does not close under binomial/trinomial relations alone and requires stronger ideal-membership evidence (e.g. Gröbner).
All generated supports pass independent verification (0 failures across 6561 colourings and structural checks). The elementary constraint loop is retained as an explicit baseline.

* Hunt #35 complete: OEIS A107311's two conjectures are false
The supremum of the real parts of the zeros of the prime zeta function
is sigma_c = 1.779544653546994116445898786965 (decided, both backends,
root of P(sigma) = 2^(1-sigma)), not the conjectured x* = 1.7286...
(root of zeta(x) = 2, the partial-sums-of-zeta constant). Separation
decided > 1/20. The subset conjecture fails without bound: {p >= 3}
out-walls the full series, and tail subsets {p >= p_k} have walls
growing like log2(p_k) (decided instance at p = 23).
Full proofs in THEOREM.md (wall by triangle inequality; existence by
Bohr-Kronecker-Rouche with an aggregated-tail polygon, closed with no
undischarged assumption; unboundedness via Rosser-Schoenfeld (3.8),
re-checked against the paper). Calibration control reproduces the
Borwein et al. partial-sums constant to 31 digits through the same
solver. All four preregistered predictions held. One instrument defect
(iv endpoints collapsed through the global mp context) was caught by
kill condition 3, fixed, documented, and re-run clean.

* Hunt #36 gate: four adversaries, prior art, and the NOT YET verdict
The mathematics survived every attack, including independent
recomputations of both sides. Two major defects stand in the
surroundings:
- Frame: the hunt's deformation sits at s = 1/2 + iz, while de Bruijn,
Newman, Rodgers-Tao, Polymath 15 and Dobner all sit at s = (1+iz)/2.
Dobner's deformation is H_{t/4}(z/2), so Lambda(their frame) = 4
Lambda(hunt frame). THEOREM13.md section 6 asserts the two share
Lambda exactly, which is false by that factor. In the common frame
the bracket reads 0.2304 < Lambda_DH <= 1.6025.
- winding.py justifies the evenness step that makes M2 a bound at all
by a statement that is false as written (the summand is not termwise
even); the conclusion is true from the functional equation, and a
deflated-M2 lesion shows the one unguarded analytic step returns a
wrong integer rather than refusing.
Prior art: no source attaches a number to a de Bruijn-Newman constant
of any RH-violating function, so the bracket survives as original, but
Stopple (arXiv:1301.3158) already publishes this exact normalization
and a quantitative non-zeta constant, and Bombieri-Ghosh 2011 is unread
and is the likeliest place in print for the strip constant.

* Hunt #36 hardening: upper bound sharpened 2.082x in-tree, M2 proved, prior art closed
All three pre-submission items landed. The lower bound and the separation
did not move in any digit.
Upper bound. The coefficient-domination strip was the free-phase
relaxation: it replaces each n^{-it} by an independent worst case, and the
phases are multiplicative. Used quantitatively, a zero with Re s > 1 forces
a fixed total argument on the ratio of the two Dirichlet L-functions of the
odd character mod 5, while each prime p = 2, 3 mod 5 supplies at most
2 arctan(p^{-sigma}) radians of it, the argument-maximising point of the
Moebius image disc having modulus exactly 1. The abscissa where the primes
run out decides on both backends at sigma_0' = 1.12036249819, giving
narrow. The tail is closed by the Euler products themselves, with the k >= 2
corrections cancelling at every even k, so no prime-counting estimate enters.
This is Bombieri-Ghosh's Theorem 7 equation term for term, but only its
necessary half is used and that half is derived here: the number is theirs,
the grade is ours. The bracket ratio falls 6.955 to 3.341.
Recorded as failing, since it was the obvious route: period-5 block
regrouping with the mean value theorem is correct but carries a factor |s|,
so it yields a height-restricted strip that climbs back to the old constant,
and de Bruijn's theorem consumes a half-plane statement.
M2 is proved (M2-LEMMA.md), every constant a reported ball, exercised by
four routes and two falsification attacks. What survives of the blind spot
is narrower and still disclosed: the detector cannot see a corrupted M2 by
itself and its health metric moves the wrong way across the lesion.
Prior art closed. The 403-walled academia.edu preprint was read in full via
its Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.21679490, Mesut Ismail): Davenport-
Heilbronn appears there only as instrument and negative control, it names no
de Bruijn-Newman constant for it, and its nearest numbers are two-zero upper
bounds pointing the wrong way for a lower bound. It independently states
this hunt's factor-4 frame dictionary, so FRAME.md now has an outside
source. Bombieri-Mueller 2008 identified and not a threat; the Dobner
forward-citation sweep re-run across independent indexes.
Two in-tree corrections: BOMBIERI-GHOSH.md's re-solves sat on the wrong side
of their own root by about 1e-17, and FRAME.md's 18-digit row derived from
one of them.

AGENTS.md gains two habits, both earned this session. Look before you report:
git fetch and call list_sessions before describing repository state, because

22f4be9963aa5828958570674f7c8f4bc5abcad4.subject: hunts/r_8c3b94: price both routes to Erdős–Kac, and find one of them blocked
22f4be9963aa5828958570674f7c8f4bc5abcad4.body: A mapping run, not a proving run. Two earlier runs left Erdős–Kac as prose;
files: this one turns it into coordinates, resolving every Mathlib claim by compiling
43 #checks against the pinned toolchain rather than by grep.
The moment method comes to roughly 2,400 to 3,700 lines of Lean, ~1,800 to
2,600 of them novel, with the reindexing of k-tuples of primes by set-partition
as the hardest step and the widest band. The characteristic-function route is
not merely dearer: it is blocked on the fundamental lemma of sieve theory,
which Mathlib lacks (its Selberg sieve is upper-bound only) and which has no
Lean formalization. The sieve-free variant closes on itself, because the
characteristic function needs all orders at once and so carries an error of
2^(pi(y)), which forces y down to about log N, where loglog y stops being
asymptotic to loglog N. The moment route needs only k-fold products, error
pi(y)^k, and survives at y = N^(1/2k). That one asymmetry is the finding.
Also corrects prior prose in this tree: hunts/r_0339c1 treats tightening the
Mertens band 16 as the lever, which is true for the Hardy-Ramanujan constant
275 and irrelevant to Erdős–Kac, whose moment route uses the band only as an
O(1) shift divided by sqrt(loglog N). A prerequisite that looked live is dead.
Recommendation handed back: fund the moment route or nothing, starting with
the k=4 central moment as a single bounded file with a stated stop condition.
Three sub-obligations are wanted upstream independently of whether Erdős–Kac
is ever attempted.
Nothing here is evidence for or against RH (docs/08). Case-log entry #48.

8789d2295539b5064cef7418696bfbae9efac723.body: `reNum_mem` and `imNumOverY_mem` pin the shapes the interval arithmetic
files: computes, with the three constant leaves left abstract. Whether those shapes
are `Re num` and `Im num / y` was unproved in either direction. New file
`Zeta23Ext/EForm3/O9NumShape.lean` settles it, and the two sides answer
differently.
`reNum` encloses `Re num` unconditionally: instantiate the constants at
`SQ2_mem` / `SINC_mem` / `COSC_mem` and the computed shape is the real part,
at every point of every box including `y = 0`, with no hypothesis beyond the
ones the leaves already carried.
`imNumOverY` encloses `Im num / y` only for `y != 0`. The hypothesis is
necessary, not incidental, and the witness is in the file: `Im num` vanishes
on the real axis, so `Im num / y` at `y = 0` is `0` by Lean's division
convention, while the field carries `shcSmall` and therefore encloses the
removable limit, which is `2*cos(sqrt2/2) + sqrt2*sin(sqrt2/2) > 0` at
`s = pi`. That asymmetry is the design working rather than a defect: the
removable branch exists so `y = 0` is an ordinary point, and it can only be
ordinary by enclosing something other than a quotient by `y` there.
With both components identified, `qreIv_mem_phi2` and `rIv_mem_phi2` read the
two compositions back against `Phi2` itself.
Verdict on the dead weight run 4df2ee65 found: `O9Seam.r_comp_mem` and
`Retention.rIv_mem` can be retired at no reproof cost. `r_comp_mem` has one
use site (`rIv_mem`) and `rIv_mem` has none; the route here goes through
`r_comp_mem'` and `rIv_mem_box`. Shown unnecessary, not deleted.
27 declarations, zero sorrys, `lake build Zeta23Ext.EForm3.Main` green
(8726 jobs), `#print axioms` reporting only propext / Classical.choice /
Quot.sound and, for `box0_in_table`, no axioms at all. Because a compiling
lemma is not a lemma with content, every identification is also instantiated
at the first recorded row of `o9boxes` at the interior point `(23/4, 1/8)`
with every hypothesis discharged.
Not claimed: O9 soundness is not closed. The two-mode arithmetic and the
identity joining `Phi2` to `EForm3.Qre`/`Qim` are separate and untouched, and
the `y = 0` mismatch witness sits outside the table's `s`-range. Two
pre-existing build failures (`RetentionWired.lean:44`, and `BandCert.Verify`
killed at 704 s) are recorded in RESULTS.md rather than absorbed. Nothing
here is evidence for or against RH.

f3b755d37f701c6a950e65a6a0371def42def21e.subject: lean(r_4218d4): tighten the Mertens chain, 5855 -> 275
f3b755d37f701c6a950e65a6a0371def42def21e.body: The Turan variance constant of ZetaLean.HardyRamanujan.sum_sq_dev_le was
files: 76^2 + 76 + 3, where 76 is the Mertens II band and that in turn rounds a
chain starting at mertens_first_theorem's log 4 + 16. The dependence is
quadratic, so the whole lever is upstream. Three local steps, no new
mathematics, every statement's shape preserved.
1. The Chebyshev remainder. Mathlib's Chebyshev.psi_le gives
psi x <= x log 4 + 2 sqrt(x) log x and its packaged corollary bounds
the remainder by 4x, i.e. by log t / sqrt t <= 2, where the supremum
is 2/e. A new lemma log_le_div_exp_one (log t <= t/e, which is
log x <= x - 1 applied at x = t/e) gives (4/e)x; psi_le_const_mul_self'
states psi x <= (log 4 + 3/2) x for x >= 1.
2. sum_log_div_sq_le, 6 -> 3/2. The same majorant replaces log n <= 2 sqrt n,
and the vanishing n = 1 term is dropped so the telescope starts at 2,
where sum n^(-3/2) <= 2 rather than 3. The prime-power tail is 2B, so
3. Mertens I is asymmetric: its lower half loses 1, its upper half the
whole Chebyshev constant, and routing the prime form through the
symmetric von Mangoldt band paid both. A one-sided
log_sub_one_le_sum_vonMangoldt_div keeps them apart, worth 1.5.
Then propagation, with 1/log 2 < 2 also sharpened to < 1.443:
mertens_first_theorem   log 4 + 16  ->  log 4 + 3
mertens_second_theorem          76  ->  16
No statement weakened, no hypothesis added, no sorry. Every theorem in the
chain still reports exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; the
audit script is hunts/r_4218d4/PrintMertensAxioms.lean. The classical
constants (2 and 4) remain out of reach and were not chased; what is left
is priced in hunts/r_4218d4/RESULTS.md, where the largest single term is
now the log 4 of Chebyshev's bound, whose removal is the prime number
theorem rather than a constant tightening.
Nothing here bears on RH (docs/08).

50df26a0a7b72fe50f91c1f120c6dcb38189bd7d.subject: hunts/r_b9552d: where the centre-gas obligation T1 resists, measured
50df26a0a7b72fe50f91c1f120c6dcb38189bd7d.body: Probe of K2-TWO-SPECIES.md section 5's first obligation. k >= 3 is not
files: closed, T1 is not proved, the reading of record does not move.
Three findings.
1. T1 restates exactly against a budget that is already proved. Splitting
gram_form.budget_gram's Gram sums into diagonal and off-diagonal parts
gives GAS = k*Shq(y) - 2B + P with P the positive-part credit the
D <= Dam step discards (residual 8.0e-15 over 300 configurations).
B >= 0 follows from Retention.energy_F_ge, so T1 with signed damage and
rho = 0 is a consequence of a kernel-checked theorem, and the whole
content of T1 is the strict positivity of rho together with P.
2. The atom reserve has a closed-form ceiling. T1 holds with reserve rho
iff rho*k*Shq <= 2B - P; on the critical 2*pi lattice P = 0 (measured to
d = 4000) and B/k -> c2(0) - A^2 exactly by defect #24, so
against Lean's proved budget floor. This replaces the measured 87.8%
of the per-centre budget. It is a ceiling, not a floor.
3. Three searches for the gas extremum all return the uniform 2*pi
lattice: exhaustive periodic occupancy for periods up to 14 over 230
spacings, free periodic with up to 8 free positions in a free period,
and free finite k. Best row 0.05716 against the budget 0.06751. The
planted-fault ladder first reports a violation at 1.20x damage against
a 1.18x measured margin, so the verdict has demonstrated power.
Also: NAMED_GAPS G4's 1,1,2,1,1,2,3 row of 0.1200, the only recorded
evidence against lattice extremality, did not reproduce under any of three
readings (0.0666 / 0.0902 / -1.3600 against the lattice's 0.1143). Recorded
as a failure to reproduce, not adjudicated. K2-TWO-SPECIES.md amended.
Assessed and not settled: a Cohn-Elkies-style certificate for T1, distinct
from all five recorded dead routes. Its truncated LP must clear 0.05716 to
bound anything and stay under 0.06751 to work; it reached 0.05410 and the
solver failed above horizon 200.
Double precision throughout, no enclosures, no Lean. Nothing here is
evidence for or against RH (docs/08).

09745f72e996aaba2e4f4aa9bfc7f2a03d9d83af.subject: r_b9552d run 2: gap A of the lattice-extremality route is a forbidden constant (#63)
09745f72e996aaba2e4f4aa9bfc7f2a03d9d83af.body: Second run of this hunt. Run 1's artifacts are preserved verbatim under
files: run-tagged names; nothing it settled is re-derived and nothing it said is
contradicted. Two of its four threads were answered on main between the runs
(a735965 withdrew the G4 counterexample, 7efd506 closed gap B), so this run
starts where that leaves the obligation: gap A, the sparse side.
The result is a pinning, not a search. Any single density-independent
Cohn-Elkies certificate g (g >= f, ghat <= 0) proving J <= L at every density
has all four of its constants forced at once:
ghat(0) = 0,  g(0) = -L/2,  sup|g| <= L/2,  ghat = 0 on all of Z.
Two tests follow. The necessary condition sup f <= L/2 PASSES, with margin
the route is not excluded; a 3.05x planted inflation of f fires the test, so
the test has power. But the Fejer family that closed gap B reaches ghat(0)=0
only at c = 2*c2(0) = 1.6984559986, where the bound becomes exactly L at
every density (spread 6.7e-16), and admissibility caps c at
frequency witness ghat(0.87493) = +0.0839055 > 0.
The route document already records c < 2*c2(0) as the reason LP_v "stays
decreasing". The reading it does not draw is that decreasing IS the failure
mode: 2*c2(0) is exactly the boundary between a bound that decays with
density and one that is uniform in it, and ghat <= 0 sits 15.55% below it.
Byproduct, and the first sparse-side bound in this route: spending the
largest admissible c instead of the smallest gives J(T) <= 0.5715840116 for
EVERY periodic configuration at EVERY density, 4.99942 * L. Five times the
truth, so no evidence of extremality, but it holds where the route previously
said nothing.
Measured, double precision, no enclosures, no Lean. Nothing here bears on RH
(docs/08). No ledger entry was made and the negative check is recorded in
RESULTS.md section 6: standing_reasons is empty for both ledger claims,
unguarded() is empty, undemonstrated() names only tests/test_doors.py, and
review_ledger's own policy is that a live frontier thread is not entered.

e87dc9239bfec4bab05e97c6493c991f85f1717b.subject: hunts/r_233abe: bridge omega to Mathlib's omega, and the pointwise Hardy-Ramanujan
e87dc9239bfec4bab05e97c6493c991f85f1717b.body: Closes both threads run 43d363c1 left in
files: lean/ZetaLean/HardyRamanujantheorem.lean. Zero sorrys, axioms unchanged
(propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), no existing statement, constant or
proof weakened or edited. The file grows 384 -> 588 lines.
The bridge. omega n = ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors n is rfl, but not
because the two are the same spelling: this file counts n.primeFactors.card and
Mathlib counts n.primeFactorsList.dedup.length, and Nat.primeFactors is
primeFactorsList.toFinset, so the two unfold to the same term. The docstring now
names the two definitions it identifies instead of asserting they are one. A
one-line rfl is a restated definition, so the bridge is carried through to
hardy_ramanujan_cardDistinctFactors, in which omega, loglog, exceptional and
HardyRamanujanTheorem are all unfolded away: every name in that statement is
Mathlib's, and an ArithmeticFunction-facing development can cite the theorem
without importing anything from this namespace.
The pointwise form. hardy_ramanujan_pointwise measures each n against its own
log log n rather than the common log log N. Split (0, N] by n*n <= N: below the
split there are at most Nat.sqrt N integers; above it N < n*n forces
log N < 2 log n, so log log N - log 2 < log log n <= log log N and the gap
between the two normalisations is the constant log 2, uniformly in N. A
deviation of eps*log log n then forces one of eps*log log N - (eps+1)*log 2,
which is at least (eps/2)*log log N once log log N has outgrown the slack, and
hardy_ramanujan at eps/2 closes it. No new arithmetic enters: the variance
bound, its constant 275 and the Mertens band 16 are consumed as they stand, so
the pointwise form inherits any future sharpening of the density form.

green: lake build over the whole package is not, in this container -
ZetaLean.Pub1.CertL2 and ZetaLean.Pub1.CertAtoms log failures. Neither imports
anything from ZetaLean.HardyRamanujan, so neither can be a consequence of this
edit; the cause was not diagnosed.

files: v4.33.0-rc2, which carries no Mertens prime-sum statement of its own
(Wikidata Q1196729, wanted and unbuilt).
What compiles, all with explicit constants, all for N >= 1:
- the summatory identity sum_{n<=N} log n = sum_{d<=N} Lambda(d) floor(N/d)
- Mertens first, von Mangoldt form: |sum Lambda(n)/n - log N| <= log 4 + 4
- Mertens first, prime form: |sum (log p)/p - log N| <= log 4 + 16
The argument is elementary throughout: vonMangoldt_sum plus multiple
counting, Chebyshev.psi_le_const_mul_self, an induction from
log(1+1/M) <= 1/M in place of Stirling, and a telescoping n^(-3/2)
bound for the prime-power correction.
The second theorem is route-mapped but not built; the exact remaining
obstruction (one discrete partial-summation block) and the Mathlib
declarations relied on and sought are recorded in
hunts/r_3c1cbb/RESULTS.md. Case log entry: Hunt #30.

21d8e8cef2d62beeb1ab8eecaca3479201b38028.subject: Hunt #8: where the fog enters — is the ineffectivity extractable or essential?
21d8e8cef2d62beeb1ab8eecaca3479201b38028.body: Opened after the operator asked why the crossover caveat has to be
files: inherited. 'Inherited' currently functions as an explanation and is not
one, so the hunt asks where the fog enters and whether it has to.
Two facts already in the tree suggest it may not. PROOF-LEDGER blocker 3
residual (i) records that four existential EvBound constants would make
the chain effective and nothing else in the budget would - the
ineffectivity is localised, not diffuse, and the dominant error term is
already derived from parts at 35.519106. And upstream those facts are
ASSUMPTIONS: fields of a Facts structure carrying the paper's own
references, shaped as exists C > 0, exists T0, forall T >= T0, |f| <= C g,
whose docstring says 'explicit inequality with named constants, no
filter-o(1) until the final liminf wrapper'. The constants were not lost
to an obstruction; they were never carried across an interface, because
the source's goal was a limit statement.
Both verdicts are worth having, and the negative one is the more
interesting: extractable means an effective form is arithmetic rather than
new mathematics, and would stand independently of the +1.0e-5 improvement
it was reached through - the improvement is unreachable at any computable
height, an effective constant is usable above its threshold. Essential
means the obstruction finally has a name and a location.
Placed per the conventions rather than wherever: hunts/<name>/MISSION.md
with a validated huntspec block, and an entry in the README case log,
which is what tests/test_hunt_probe_discipline.py enforces - it caught the

clean. Nothing measured yet and nothing here is a result.

a311a6f265ff52777c7510bbe29416cd991b89d6.subject: lean: hprime is unprovable as stated, and the gate it guards is retargeted
a311a6f265ff52777c7510bbe29416cd991b89d6.body: Phase A on LEAN-FRONTIER item 19. Two independent derivation attempts and one
files: adversarial pass agree, and the negative half is the more useful half.
WHY THE STATED GATE CANNOT CLOSE. The insertion recurrence is asymptotically
tight. Measured X from 10^2 to 10^7 by SPF sieve with exact enumeration of
every squarefree support: (j+1)(2j)(2j+1)A_{j+1}/A_j is maximal at j = 1 at
every cutoff, strictly decreasing in j, and r_1 = 12A_2/A_1 =
(log X)^2 - 2 log X + O(1) = (1-o(1))(1+log X)^2. The extremal family is pairs
{p,q} with pq near X, with the Beta(2,2) split profile of the weight. Measured
D for B*(X) <= D(1+log X)^2 climbs monotonically 0.383 -> 0.724; a
linear-in-log envelope is refuted outright. So the order is exactly right and
any absolute D must be >= 1 — which means hprime needs an order-uniform LOWER
bound on A_j with a matching constant. Chebyshev is an upper bound, and
separate upper/lower routes inherit a (C/c)^j mismatch incompatible with an
absolute D. Dead route, mechanism recorded.
WHAT SURVIVES. Nothing downstream consumes the recurrence — RAMS2-CLUSTER §6
uses only the endpoint display, and the display survives domination. So the
gate becomes a plain domination against the explicit majorant
M_j = c B^{j-1} X (1+log X)^{2j+1}/(j!(2j-1)!), which satisfies the insertion
recurrence WITH EQUALITY at B(1+log X)^2: the factorial denominator is built
so that (j+1)(2j)(2j+1) is exactly denominator(j+1)/denominator(j). The
tightness that defeats hprime on the true masses is precisely the equality the
majorant enjoys.
MajorantBypass.lean, kernel-checked, zero sorrys, lint-clean:
mass_le_of_dominated_majorant     domination + recurrence -> the display
powerMajorant_step                the equality, exactly
distinctPrimeLogMass_le_of_dominated  the concrete bypass
simplexFactorialDenominator_succ was NOT re-proved: a first draft duplicated
it before finding it already in WeightedSimplex.
The remaining formal obligation is now exactly one hypothesis, hdom : A_j <=
powerMajorant, which is not tight and is what RAMS1-ATTACK §4.2 already
sketches on paper. Both routes proved it there by integral comparison in log
coordinates; route A gives D = log 16 = 2.7726 and is the one to formalise
(route B's 60 log 4 = 83.18 is 30x worse). Every intermediate inequality of
both chains verified numerically at X = 250 and X = 5000.
lake build: 8739 jobs, zero sorrys.

8be1eee941cba4be41c9d649b33945c7c6b6cbff.body: These existed only in a transient agent transcript. LEAN-FRONTIER item 20
files: carried the one-paragraph conclusion; this is the working a later session needs
in order to formalise anything, and losing it would have cost a re-derivation.
HPRIME-ROUTES.md carries, for both independent chains: every lemma statement,
its per-link formalisation cost, and the numeric margin measured for it at
Route A (one-shot Stieltjes domination, D = log 16 = 2.7726) is the one to
formalise. L1, L2, L10 and Theorem R are already in the kernel; L3, L5, L8 are
routine; L4 (discrete Abel against a piecewise-constant comparison) and L6
(Fubini on a triangle plus the Beta step) are the real work and are exactly
what the token-constraint record tells a weaker model not to start.
Route B (marked deletion, one-dimensional Abel, induction on j,
D = 60 log 4 = 83.178) is kept for two reasons despite the 30x worse constant:
its analysis never forms a j-fold integral, which is a genuine formalisation
advantage if L4/L6 prove worse in Lean than estimated, and its obstruction
argument is independent and sharper.
That obstruction is the thing I had not captured. Route B does not merely fail
to reach the literal gate — it establishes that NO subset-local charging scheme
can reach it with B = O((1+log X)^2): pairs with both primes below sqrt(X) must
be absorbed by singletons below sqrt(X), which forces
12*A_2^small/A_1(sqrt X) <= B(X), and that ratio grows like sqrt(X)/log X.
Measured 0.097 at X=250, 0.56 at 5000, 2.54 at 10^5, 7.36 at 10^6: it crosses
1 near X ~ 2e4 and diverges. Route A's independent argument is that the
inequality is irreducibly aggregate and that two-sided elementary Chebyshev
loses 2^j over j up to ~log X/log log X, so the literal gate needs
PNT-with-error-term strength absent from the pinned Mathlib.
Scope kept honest: the impossibility holds for the local-transport class only.
A non-local elementary argument is not excluded, though nothing here points to
one. The literal statement is numerically true with 4-5x margin at both tested
cutoffs and is recorded as a conjecture, not a theorem.

b87ee6b14dc315048095b957148f4300fb505233.subject: hunt: a cross-arm transfer proposal, its own direction error, and the measurement that beat it
b87ee6b14dc315048095b957148f4300fb505233.body: Two arms hit the same obstruction shape independently, days apart, and both killed
files: it with a measured crossing rather than an argument: higher_xi's subset-local
charging (crossing at X ~ 2e4) and frontier_math's per-pair domination (a
four-pair lattice where the sum of single-pair caps already exceeds budget). Both
surviving reformulations are also the same move — comparison against a fixed
nonnegative autocorrelation kernel — and local_positivity found a third instance
independently (Q_p as a norm at every place). Recorded as an observation about
method.
The transfer proposed: frontier_math's open step (verdict on 320 tested
configurations, not all) has the shape higher_xi was stuck on, and this arm got out
by a majorant whose recurrence is an IDENTITY rather than by any slack argument —
kernel-checked as MajorantBypass.mass_le_of_dominated_majorant.
Then the test was run, and two corrections came out of it, both kept rather than
edited away:
1. The direction in section 3 is WRONG. The frontier verdict needs a lower bound
on the exponential sum, so a minorant, not a majorant.
2. The measurement is more useful than the proposal. The whole universality
question is one competition in the arm's own decomposition, budget = sum_slack
+ pair_term. The 2-pair worst case sits at gap d ~ 6.640 with both depths at
the shallow limit, where sum_slack/|pair_term| = 4.16 and the ratio is flat in
y — agreeing with the arm's homogeneity argument and putting a number on its
limit. And the k^2 fear does not materialise: only the nearest-neighbour gap
contributes negatively, so pair_term turns positive by k = 4 and the budget
rises monotonically with more pairs.
If the binding case really is k = 2, multi-pair universality stops being an
infinite-dimensional configuration problem and becomes a three-parameter compact
one in (d, y1, y2) — closable by grid plus interval arithmetic rather than
majorised around.
Flagged as the reason to distrust it first: that reading would make an open step
easy, and it does not reconcile with the arm's own random search, which recorded a
worst budget of 0.2907 while the shallow 2-pair limit measures 0.0000942 — four
orders apart. Either the search never reached the shallow limit or I have misread
which margin the verdict consumes. The document says to resolve that before
trusting any of it.
Not promoted, and aimed at another arm which owns the decision.

127c6ba4cce070d801adb449e429b41b75b8c498.body: The interaction-control audit closed with one admissible next task: an
files: unconditional zeta constraint, at the pinned paper's own window/grid
interface, that rejects the exact obstruction family defeating every
universal strengthening of the rank-trace step.
Derived and measured here, all from the complex extension of the paper's
no-aliasing Poisson-Gabor identity (Lemma 2.2):
- LAW D: the bilinear self-incidence of every zero equals aL^2 at every
depth and position, so each off-line pair carries bilinear trace +2m_rho
on the full grid; the family's bad pair declares -2m^2 (exact integer
margin 2m^2+2).
- LAW E: the imaginary mass aL^2 sigma^2(y) is alias-free, giving a signed
two-sided envelope on every subgrid and the per-cell lower envelope
2 Re(Bhat^2) >= -2 sigma^2(y); negative incidence mass requires depth.
- LAW F: sigma^2(y) <= sinh^2(yL/2) and the unconditional strip bound cap
realisable members at m < sigma(1/2-): at L = 8 every m >= 2 dies at
every placement, and the theta -> 0 defeat is floored at an explicit
positive value per bandwidth.
Controls: truncation ladders (defects 1.7e-13 -> 5.4e-19), an aliasing
lesion whose defect does not respond to refinement, a planted-wrong decoy,
random-subgrid envelope scans with no violation, and the Davenport-
Heilbronn rival check at its pinned off-line depth. Honest scope recorded:

584714c2f6a90b6e73e5f6104b9a1f5f8af00b96.subject: Answer the marked two-gap coexistence question: no, and why
584714c2f6a90b6e73e5f6104b9a1f5f8af00b96.body: The directive's immediate question was whether one off-line pair can
files: simultaneously realise the worst signed incidence level 1 allows across
two consecutive on-line gaps. The answer is no, for a sharper reason
than incompatible offsets: the level-1 envelope is not attained in even
one cell.
Everything follows from one exact split. Writing Phi2(g+iy) = C - iS,
the parity of phi^2 kills the mixed terms and leaves
W(g,y) = 2(C^2 - S^2)/(aL)^2 with C even and S odd in both arguments -
which is Phase 1's translation covariance, its rho <-> 1-conj(rho)
symmetry, and the shared kernel column, all as identities.
Saturating level 1 needs C = 0 and equality in Cauchy-Schwarz, i.e.
sin(gu) proportional to sinh(yu) on the support; matching Taylor
coefficients forces g(g^2 + y^2) = 0, and at g = 0 we get S = 0 and a
positive cell value. So no cell ever sits at the floor.
LAW I (proved, uniform): sharpening the same Cauchy-Schwarz against
sin^2 gives W >= -sigma^2(1 - omega(2g)) >= -(1 + m0) sigma^2 with the
window constant m0 = -min omega = 0.2137172540, so every cell carries a
uniform factor 2/(1+m0) = 1.6478 of slack against the level-1 envelope.
LAW J (exact): for a periodic word at critical spacing the density of
Phi2(.+iy)^2 vanishes at the dual points, so Poisson leaves only m = 0
and sum_k W = 2b/a^2 = 2.2959062623, independent of depth and ordinate.
The periodic near-obstruction lesion gets no negativity at all.
Phases 2/3 collapse, and the collapse is the finding: W is even in g,
so a mirror pair at gap 2g* realises twice the single-cell minimum with
penalty below 4e-13, and clusters at spacing delta -> 0 realise n times
it. Coexistence alone therefore yields no positive penalty (OUTCOME B),
and the escaping family is pinned exactly (OUTCOME C): the +-g* cluster,
a near-multiple zero controlled only by density and multiplicity. No LP
was built, because its value is known to be zero on that family.
Phase 5 comes from LAW I with no coexistence input: no cell is within
(1-m0) sigma^2 of the level-1 floor, so the margin is linear in n.
Phase 6's gate is not passed and no decimal search is opened.
Lesions: independent cells buy the adversary 0.3827; conjugate-transpose
geometry destroys every sign; broken spacing moves the periodic identity
by 3.5e-2; independent depths is recorded as a negative lesion, since
mixing never beats using the deeper depth twice.

a39cd237987db3178fa4a39ddd7ce51ae047a8de.subject: Confidence audit: separate what is cross-checked from what is assumed
a39cd237987db3178fa4a39ddd7ce51ae047a8de.body: Asked whether the reading is certain. It is not, and the reasons are now
files: written down and pinned as tests.
T3 is not a detail, it is the load-bearing unknown. The formula
H + 2*theta*c_u splits cleanly: the coefficient 2 and the linearity ARE
calibrated - H + 2*floor reproduces Cheer-Goldston's printed 1993
constant from their own inputs (recomputed floor 0.00012638 vs their
0.00012636; constant 0.6727535 vs their 0.6727534). But that theta
enters the formula MULTIPLICATIVELY is derived nowhere. CG's improvement
is RH-conditional in Montgomery's pair-correlation framework; theta is a
retention in the paper's Frobenius framework. If a retention in the
second does not plug into the arithmetic of the first, the reading is
vacuous regardless of how large theta is.
The window identification rests on exactly one number, now checked: the
pinned constant IS the Montgomery-Taylor constant, 2 - MT_CONST =
0.67250070368, matching the pinned digits to 2e-11 (pure rounding). That
is real evidence and it is the only evidence. Checking it caught two
stale repo comments printing wrong digits for MT_CONST and H_PAPER - one
of which this session had already copied into reconnect.py, asserting a
nonexistent 2e-8 gap. Corrected; both facts are now tests.
Defects of our own found and corrected in this session: the
blanket-margin artifact (three times, three guises), a theta = 1
convention mislabel, the kernel-pairing mix, and the propagated stale
comment. Every one was caught by a control or an independent route, none
by inspection - which is the argument for the controls and equally the
argument against confidence in any step no control has touched.
What survives even if T3 fails: the MT-window results themselves, which
are statements about the window and are cross-checked several ways. What
they are not is a proportion. 41 controls green.

1d2d9566e2491d7bdba15cac848915d46dcfe0bb.body: A fresh-clone adversarial audit of the 0.6725106958 candidate, run
files: against the source paper's own §3-§4 rather than against this hunt's
documents.
Findings:
- No error in the algebra. Re-deriving from Proposition 4.4 shows the
improvement over the paper is exactly R + 2 tr(P1 Q'), and that the
4-per-pair term appears identically in both routes -- it is not a
double count, and it is not the source of the gain.
- The pair-pair term is load-bearing and belongs on the right of the
retention inequality. It equals the joint dual's T_signed exactly;
that dictionary entry was missing and is now measured (rel. defects
3.5e-5 .. 1.4e-3 at K=1200, the assembly's own 1/K).
- identification_seam.end_to_end's SHARP row omits that term from the
left. Re-run including it, all eleven configurations still hold --
but the battery's binding rows are single-pair, where the term is
identically zero, so the battery does not corroborate the joint
dual where it matters.
- PaperBandDual at its shipped step 5e-4 reports a NEGATIVE verdict at
y = 5e-4 and finds no bands below y ~ 1e-4 while its own control
says the cover is not clear. Refining the step to 5e-6 moves the
ratio 1.436 -> 0.493, converging to the same ~0.49 seen at y = 0.02:
a slope-margin artifact of the coarse grid, not a failure of the
inequality -- but the instrument is unusable at shallow depth.
The open obligation, stated exactly: the retention inequality is a
genuine one-sided supremum over on-line configurations, established at
four sampled depths in Q and over swept pair families. Uniformity in
the depth and over arbitrary pair sets is unproved, and without it the
kernel-checked corollary's hypothesis D >= theta*R0 is unavailable.
Also recorded: the Lean skeleton assumes unit vectors, while the
paper's truncated vectors have norm <= 1, so the conclusion carries
2 tr P rather than 2N -- exactly the o(N) that seam (i) owes.

c370a2f03d61d09c26dc034daeb9ebbd42386602.body: Derive the unit dictionary into the source paper's hat units - one
files: change of variable and one Poisson lemma read at two step sizes - and
find the conversion factor is exactly 1: the normalised Gram is
grid-step independent because the 2pi/h cancels between inner product
and normalisation. a equals our A bit-identically. The transfer then has
a clean form purely in upstream objects, since ||P||_F^2 = sum m^2 + R
exactly.
The error budget corrects the natural guess: calE is not the leading
term, the window-moment drift is, with a constant derived from parts
(35.519106) that matches measurement to four digits and whose partial
derivative is -HD'(1) as it must be.
The verdict has two halves and both are the result. The improvement does
NOT drown - it is a fixed constant against o(1) errors, so the composed
statement is the same logical type as the source's own epsilon-form. But
it is NOT numerically effective at any reachable height: the crossover
sits at T ~ 10^(1.7e6), and the shape T0 ~ exp(38.5/improvement) is
inherited from the source's own o(1) coefficients rather than introduced
by the transplant. Anyone reading "improvement" as "better at computable
heights" would be wrong.

floor rises as lambda falls. Named residual: theta is measured at

f78127b8b9ae78531a14ac15947df91c791e0484.subject: Blocker 2 stays open: the per-pair route is refuted
f78127b8b9ae78531a14ac15947df91c791e0484.body: The route this coordinator proposed for multi-pair universality does not
files: work, and the refutation is the deliverable. Subadditivity holds at the
field level exactly as expected but does not survive the square
completion: the joint cap exceeds the sum of single-pair caps by up to
3.4x for coincident stacks, with an exact closed-form excess, because
the adversary collects k times the damage from a stack while paying the
internal charge once. The band set is not what moves - it is the
occupancy.
The decisive part is that the route could not have worked at all: from
three pairs on a unit lattice, the sum of single-pair caps already
exceeds the budget while the joint verdict closes with 40 percent
margin. The joint field's shielding is load-bearing, so no per-pair
argument can reach theta = 0.995 in either direction. The slack the
brief assumed additive is not additive either; its pair term is signed
and erodes 84 percent of a pair's slack on the worst lattice.
Both repairs fail for stated reasons. What survives is better posed than
what it replaces: the whole verdict restates as a single bandlimited
nonnegative-kernel inequality in two exponential sums. Randomised search
over 320 configurations opened nothing and rediscovered the binding
family blind - evidence, labelled as evidence.

a957678900ed4d7daabe966965e7f718ebf87f27.subject: Two research-grade prover results: pair energy proved sharp, E-form partial
a957678900ed4d7daabe966965e7f718ebf87f27.body: Unlike the four earlier Lean artifacts, these were open statements - we
files: had numerics and no proof, and asked the service to prove or refute.
PairEnergy.lean closes the pair half of the E-form obligation sharply:
for the bandlimited kernel of the paper window, the cosh-weighted
exponential-sum energy is at least 4k for every k and ALL real depths
and positions. The two hypotheses we asked for turned out unnecessary
and were dropped, and the constant is attained so it cannot be
improved. The proof is an inertia argument on the Gram matrix of the
exponentials against the nonnegative window weight, closed by trace
Cauchy-Schwarz with a regularisation rather than spectral theory.
EForm/ is an honest partial on the single-pair retention inequality at
the exact constants: an exact reduction valid for every configuration,
the inequality for at most three on-line points uniformly in shift and
depth, damage localisation, and the arbitrary-n case when at most three
offsets are damaging. The unrestricted statement was not obtained and no
counterexample was found. The obstruction is recorded precisely - any
uniform-constant bound on the damage caps at n <= 2A/kappa, giving n <= 3
here and at most n <= 7 even optimally - and that is itself a finding:
it shows the band/repulsion structure of our own dual is necessary
rather than convenient.
One comment reworded for the hunts/ lexical rules, disclosed; no proof
content altered. No proportion is claimed.

e6a3a2fa8ab9e2c3f4e251b03db24338a32808a9.body: The survey recommended this library as scaffolding for the
files: finite-to-infinite bridge. Its own audit refutes that: the tree carries

wanted - PoissonSummation_Lattices - is itself a sorry inside a file
headed "SHOULD EVENTUALLY BE REMOVED", with a sorry in its hypothesis
predicate definition. Requiring it would have imported those sorrys and
made a downstream statement typecheck as an axiom-tainted lie.

needing continuity plus polynomial decay and no smoothness, which our
kernel satisfies because its corner never enters - it appears only as
the transform. And the bridge itself is now located: our own data shows
finite-m values CROSS the limit, so no one-sided lemma exists to borrow;
the tractable statement is a two-sided estimate whose discrepancy is a
boundary term over O(1) cluster-end pairs, elementary because the kernel
is compactly supported so the dual sum is already finite.

d03cd4875172cabb8f551d30a597bc6f298e01a3.subject: SOS route closed with an exact witness; bridge derived, family open, possible counterexample flagged
files: The Gram-positivity route is closed, not merely unproductive: an exact
rational family satisfies PSD, the involution relations, the diagonal
constraint and Cauchy-Schwarz while driving the objective to minus
infinity (re-checked in fractions with rational LDL). The witness is not
a realizable configuration, so the target survives - but any proof must
now use analytic properties of the transform beyond nonnegativity of the
window, coupling the on-line block to the cross block jointly rather
than entrywise. A size-independent multiplier does exist and is provably
short by exactly nk/(n+k) + theta R.
The truncation bridge is derived, including why no one-sided lemma could
ever have existed: the leading coefficient flips sign at commensurate
spacings. The rate is (a + b log m)/m, not 1/m, because the kernel corner
leaves a non-oscillating term; the derived coefficient matches the fit to
0.3 percent. The estimate holds on all 504 grid points.
But the payoff fails: m0 blows up at the resonance and at the budget
floor, and AT THE WORST POINT OF THE RHO MAP THE FINITE MARGIN GOES
NEGATIVE FROM m = 24. The budget side behaves as derived; the cap side is
the cause, and the cap is step-dependent in the direction that could make
this an artifact. Until that is resolved the multi-pair verdict at 0.995
is in doubt rather than merely unproved, and the ledger says so.

0e6ab241b1b32fec615cce5062254943ed9308f9.body: Land EForm2/ (7 modules, 1570 lines, sorry-free, standard axioms). The
files: submission quoted the earlier attempt's own obstruction back to it with
the two ingredients it named as missing, and it delivered: an exact
reduction, a clean sufficient condition on the total damage, the n <= 3
case now free of any hypothesis on the configuration or on y, and -
the first of its kind in this chain - the inequality for EVERY n under
a separation hypothesis on the on-line points.
Its far-field idea is better than the one supplied: measure the damage
against the slack rather than an absolute constant, which is what makes
the summation close.
The caveat is stated plainly in the ledger rather than buried. The

f39dc495c94888624b3069bdd4c8ec643c7cddc8.body: The retention inequality (199/200)E[F] + n/200 + 4 <= E[F+P] now holds for

margin = (4/A^2) * [ Shq(y)/2 - sum_j D(y, x_j - t)
The last term is what retention_of_damage discards when it uses E[F] >= n
instead of the identity. It is the repulsion, and it is not optional: the
discarding route's hypothesis is arithmetically false from n = 8
(8 x 4.396424e-03 > Shq/2 = 3.375420e-02), so no sharpening of the damage

such pair relieves at least gamma^2/400 with gamma = phi_r(w_max) = 0.8845197.

per-window maximum is over an INTEGER multiplicity:
net damage <= sum_k max_{m in Z>=0} [ m D_k - (gamma^2/800) m(m-1) ]
Integrality is load-bearing: over nonnegative measures the infimum is -1/200

convex relaxation of the atom constraint can close this — which is also why

slack_k = sum_p Shq(y_p)/2 - sum_p sum_a D(y_p, x_a - t_p)

The repulsion term carries no p index - paid once however many pairs there

5bb38a00847698dc2efc345c7e58207aa9101cf3.subject: The two arms compute one function: ghat(z) = Phi2(-i z)
5bb38a00847698dc2efc345c7e58207aa9101cf3.body: Found while reading BandCert/Phi.lean to copy its table pattern for the k=1
files: formalisation. This hunt grew two independent certification efforts and
neither knew about the other:
BandCert  encloses Phi2(z) = s(z+sqrt2) + s(z-sqrt2), s(u) = sin(u/2)/u,
on fixed-point interval arithmetic at 2^-64 (2283 lines, 0 sorry)
EForm3    works retention through Qre, Qim and D = Qim^2 - Qre^2, built
from ghat(z) = int cos(sqrt2 u) cosh(z u) du
They are the same function. sinh(i w/2)/(i w) = sin(w/2)/w = s(w), so
substituting z = -i w turns each ghat branch into an s branch of Phi2.
Residual over 27 curated points and a 1600-point grid: exactly 0.0 -
bit-identical, because after the rotation the closed forms are the same
expression. A = Phi2(0) to the last bit; phi_r(v) = Phi2(v) on the real axis,
which is BandCert's phiR.
Consequence for the remaining k=1 obligation. The previous ledger entry called
the damage table "the analogue of the BandCert leaf tables". It is an INSTANCE
of them:
- Phi2 at a COMPLEX point is already kernel-checked (Phi.phiC / phiC_mem)
- the complex interval layer assumed missing already exists (CIv, with
add/sub/mul/div/mulR/ofR soundness)
- D(y,s) = -Re[Phi2(s - i y)^2] is three composition steps: phiC at (s,-y),
square by CIv.mul_mem, negate the real part
7 of 12 obligations are already kernel-checked in BandCert. Of the 5 new, four
are small (the linarith reduction, the wiring lemma, the integer square
completion, two one-variable bounds on phiR) and one is the real cost: the cap
table itself.
Also lands this session's meta evidence in the intervention ledger: the
operator's bare "are you sure?" caught defects #12, #17 and #20, all with one
signature - a number relayed rather than an object derived - with the missing
capability named and falsifiable; and, as counterweight, the observation that
the one coordinator instrument error no human caught was caught by a
planted-fault control whose firing threshold matches the measured margin to
Named gaps R1-R5: the wiring lemma is on paper and checked numerically but is
NOT written in Lean, phiC_mem's y != 0 needs its own y = 0 line, the table is
NOT built, and none of this touches k >= 2. No proportion has moved and
nothing here bears on RH.

files: Two sizing attempts failed first and the failures were the method:
- requiring D <= 0 on a cell straddling a window edge is unprovable by

- capping a bracket by one wide ball gives a 6x dependency blow-up whose
cap sum 3.54e-02 already exceeds the budget 3.375e-02.
Fix: locate the true window edges, pad the brackets strictly outside them so
D < 0 with margin off-bracket, and compute caps by adaptive subdivision INSIDE
each bracket, where the cells themselves prove the cap.
At y = 1/2 over s in [5.6, 60], Arb at 128 bits: 9 windows (widths 0.960975 to
0.986001, first at 6.065319, min gap 5.182969), 9 brackets padded by 0.25 and
rounded outward to 1e-3, 143 in-bracket cells carrying caps 4.483880e-03 down
to 4.715629e-05, 53 off-bracket cells over 10 segments. Cap sum 1.319090e-02
both sides against Shq/2 = 3.375420e-02, ratio 0.3908.
196 sits inside BandCert's existing 62-248, so the remaining obligation is an
ordinary instance of a pattern this package already carries. The depth
reduction keeps it one-dimensional.
Slip caught by the module's own report: the count was written as 197 from a
scratch run that rounded brackets to nearest; soundness requires rounding
outward, which gives 196. test_stated_constants_match_the_generated_table now
pins all four counts so the prose cannot drift from the computation.
ROAD B, task 1: the damage functional has negative total integral.
-D(y,s) is the Fourier cosine transform of w -> c2(w) cosh(y w), continuous
and supported on [-1,1]. Fourier inversion at the single point w = 0 gives
int D(y,s) ds = -2 pi c2(0),  INDEPENDENT OF y
Closed form vs quadrature: diff 0.0. Truncated integral across y in [0.05,0.5]
spreads by 1.2e-05 -- flat, as the identity says. Mean collectable damage
matches n * int D / (2L) to four digits for coincident and spread atom sets.
So a pair placed at random collects NEGATIVE damage, at a rate that does not
weaken with depth; positive collection requires landing in one of the narrow
windows, which is what the k=1 accounting already controls. That is the right
shape for k >= 2, where the difficulty was that damage sums over pairs while
the repulsion is paid once.
It bounds the MEAN, and the adversary chooses placements rather than drawing
them; converting it to a bound on sum_p C(t_p) needs a count of how many t can
have C(t) large, which is not supplied. Step 1 of Road B, not Road B.

f0a30a3ee23373042d9b223fd96914ccb5726ca2.subject: frontier_math: the k-pair slack is three terms and two of them are free
f0a30a3ee23373042d9b223fd96914ccb5726ca2.body: Road B step 2. The k >= 2 difficulty was stated for two days as "the repulsion
files: is paid once while the damage sums over pairs". Rewriting the slack against the
measure c2 dw shows the difficulty is elsewhere, and isolates it.
-D(y,s) = int c2(w) cosh(yw) cos(sw) dw is the Fourier transform of a POSITIVE
measure -- c2 = g*g is the autocorrelation of a nonnegative window and cosh > 0
-- so K_y := -D(y,.) is positive definite by Bochner. Min eigenvalue 1.03e-08
over 200 random Gram matrices, -6.06e-16 over the binding structured sets.
slack_k = B(T,y) + Cross(X,T,y) + R(X)/400
B(T,y)  = int c2(w) [ cosh^2(yw) |That(w)|^2 - k ] dw
Cross   = - sum_{a,p} D(y, x_a - t_p)
R(X)    = sum_{a<b} phi_r(x_a - x_b)^2
Residual against kpair_identity's direct evaluation < 1e-12 over 40 random
instances; B against its Gram form (1/2)[G_T(2y)+G_T(0)] - k A^2 at 1e-25.
B >= 0 is FREE from a theorem already kernel-checked here: int c2 |That|^2 >=
k A^2 is energy_F_ge applied to the pair centres, cosh^2 >= 1, c2 >= 0. R >= 0
is a sum of squares since K_0(v) = phi_r(v)^2. So slack_k >= Cross, and k >= 2
reduces to the single statement B + R/400 >= sum_{a,p} D.
B is the correct budget and k*Shq/2 never was. They agree exactly at k=1 and
not otherwise: 0.1514 vs 0.3375 on ten pairs at window positions, 26.54 vs
0.2025 on six coincident. That is what the 2026-08-12 "slack additivity is
false and signed" finding actually was -- the additive budget was an artifact
of the decomposition and B has no additivity to fail. A per-pair accounting was
bounding a non-additive quantity by an additive one, which is why cluster_sdp's
factor 1.99 could never have closed regardless of how loose either side was.
Recorded as insufficient so nobody re-derives it: the Cauchy-Schwarz bound that
positive definiteness also gives, sum D <= sqrt(S_X S_T), is 18x to 111x too
weak, because it bounds |sum K| and discards that D is negative almost
everywhere. A test pins it.
Not proved: B + R/400 >= sum D is the open statement, and B's nonnegativity and
Bochner are paper-and-numerics here, not Lean. Named gaps G1-G5. k >= 2 remains
open and nothing here bears on RH.

639ab58ee4e5bde51c09c72360e1d3e33d5a914f.subject: frontier_math: the counting lemma is "at most one pair per damage window"
639ab58ee4e5bde51c09c72360e1d3e33d5a914f.body: Road B step 3. gram_form reduced k >= 2 to B + R/400 >= sum_{a,p} D and named
files: the missing piece as a count. Two measurements supply it.
THE COUNTING LEMMA. Put m atoms and j pair centres in one damage window (width
<= w_max = 0.9860008). A two-species square completion closes iff
D_1^2 <= 4 (gamma^2/800) kappa(w_max)
with D_1 = 4.396424e-03 the damage per (atom, pair), gamma^2/800 = 9.779689e-04
the atom-atom relief, and kappa(w_max) = 1.620239 the pair-pair relief. It
holds at 1.932855e-05 vs 6.338174e-03 -- margin 327.9x. kappa(w_max) is 1657x
the per-pair atom relief, and that asymmetry is the whole content: the pair
species cannot crowd.
Maximising f(m,j) = m j D_1 - m(m-1) gamma^2/800 - j(j-1) kappa(w_max) over
integers gives j=1: +7.321459e-03 at m=3 (exactly the k=1 optimum, recovered as
a slice), j=2: -3.216073, j=3: -9.670185. A second pair in the same window is
never profitable.
THE BUDGET FLOOR. B is not additive, so budget-per-pair could in principle
vanish as k grows. The worst lattice spacing at k=64 is L = 6.30, just past 2pi
where kappa is most negative (-1.82e-02). Along that family B/k runs 2.459e-2,
k = 2..256 -- it bottoms out near 6.3e-03 and turns back up. Every pair carries
a budget bounded away from zero, uniformly in k.
NOT CLOSURE. A single pair facing atoms at every one of its window peaks
collects 1.372e-02 against a floor of 6.3e-03, so R/400 stays load-bearing and
the shared-R-across-pairs question is untouched. What is gone is the unbounded
form of the worry. Named gaps C1-C5.
Test-caught slip: test_one_pair_at_every_window_peak first asserted the
full-tail figure 1.372e-02 against a nine-window sum, which is 1.2888e-02. The
claim was unaffected (both beat the floor) but the test was wrong; it now pins
both numbers and the inequality between them. Same family as the 197/196 slip -
a number carried across contexts without re-deriving it.

9b0a0b3ab9afb72bee120747642a65f84cf90872.body: Caught by checking the site model against the exact slack instead of restating
files: it. Both errors were in the counting-lemma commit; both corrected in place.
ERROR 1, a factor of 2. site_value used j(j-1) kappa(w_max) for the pair
relief. The k-pair identity sums over UNORDERED pairs, so the correct term is
j(j-1) kappa(w_max)/2. Against the exact slack: two coincident pairs relieve
1.75562102, and the model claimed 3.24047835. Everything derived from it was
inflated:
AM-GM right-hand side   6.338174e-03 -> 3.169087e-03
AM-GM margin            327.9x       -> 164.0x
kappa vs atom relief    1657x        -> 828x
ERROR 2, the logic ran the wrong way, and this is the worse one. The commit
read as though f(m,j) bounded what the adversary gains. It does not. f uses the
conservative constants, so f >= B - slack, i.e. slack >= B - f: f UNDERSTATES
the slack because it discards the budget entirely. Measured, the exact slack
exceeds f at every occupancy - by +0.025 at (m,j)=(1,1), +5.05 at (1,2), +15.06
Corrected statement: slack >= B - f, so a site is safe as soon as B >= f. At
j=1, max_m f = 7.321459e-03 against Shq/2 = 3.375420e-02, a factor 4.61. At
j>=2, f < 0 so slack >= B - f > B >= 0 outright. The conclusion that a second
pair at the same site is never the adversary's play survives both corrections,
for a different reason and at half the constants.
Third thing the check surfaced: "put m atoms and j pairs in one damage window"
is not coherent, since damage needs |x_a - t_p| >= 6.0653 and anything inside a
window of width 0.986 does none. A site is an atom cluster and a pair cluster,
each of diameter <= w_max, separated by about the peak distance 6.517. The
arithmetic was right, the description was not.
Two regression tests pin the factor against the exact pair relief and pin
slack > f at every occupancy, so neither error can return silently.

848887598730c42277d719846938e253b566c565.subject: frontier_math: the #21 correction was itself wrong (defect #22)
848887598730c42277d719846938e253b566c565.body: The previous commit's fix stated slack >= B - f. That is false. B already
files: absorbs sum_{p<q} kappa, and f subtracts j(j-1)kappa/2 again, so B - f charges
the pair relief twice. On the nine site configurations (m,j) in {1,3,5}x{1,2,3}:
slack >= B - f            6 violations of 9, every one with j >= 2
slack >= k*Shq(y)/2 - f   0 violations of 9
At (m,j) = (3,2): exact slack 1.803081 against B - f = 3.422858, short by 1.9x.
f pairs with k*Shq/2, not with B, because the identity it comes from is
slack = k*Shq/2 - sum D + R/400 + sum_{p<q} kappa. Its three steps are

957f1a7b6967dc5e45d3e7231e278d5f8c65e1c7.body: O9 was recorded as the one substantial obligation left on the k=1 chain and
files: treated as prover work. It is not: a leaf table is generated data plus a
decision procedure, the pattern BandCert already uses, so it is code generation
and can be built and validated without a Lean toolchain.
o9_leaf.py reimplements Iv.lean (flo, fhi, add, sub, neg, mul, sqr, mulInt,
divInt, widen, ofQ, ofInt, div) and Phi.lean's CIv layer operation for
operation in integers at scale 2^64, then builds phiC by the same composition.
Lean's Int / is ediv, floor for SO > 0, so Python // matches. Every fixed-point
damage enclosure contains the Arb reference at six offsets over [5.7, 59.9].
