bits. In the kernel's own arithmetic it is 344 (max depth 20, 0 undecided,
smallest margin 3.63e9 ulp = 1.97e-10). Arb is tighter than fixed point at
2^-64, so cells Arb decides need splitting again in the arithmetic that will
actually run: 196 underestimated the real Lean cost by 43%. The margin is far
above the few-ulp band where the leaf caveat would bite, so the prediction is
safe. 344 sits above BandCert's 62..248 but on the same order.
TERMINATION DETAIL. The walk must cut [28/5, 60] at every window endpoint
before subdividing: bisection never lands on one (endpoints are rationals with
denominator 10^4, midpoints are dyadic), so straddling cells shrink forever -
768 cells, 18 undecided at depth 40. With the cuts, 344 and none undecided.
Third appearance of this trap in the hunt; it now has a test.
ONE DELIBERATE REFUSAL. O9Damage.lean defines damageIv and states its soundness
lemma damageIv_mem in prose, NOT as a sorry. A placeholder would have been the
first sorry in zeta23ext, which has been sorry-free throughout and for which

fb8f73c09fcfe14a51bddfe760d8b58d9e90b75d.subject: k>=2: the budget's superadditivity, and why the per-pair route is structurally dead
fb8f73c09fcfe14a51bddfe760d8b58d9e90b75d.body: The ledger's '1.99x short on the budget side' entry is superseded a few lines
files: below it by defect #20, and a reader who stops at the first entry prices this
problem wrongly. The statement measures healthy: worst relative margin +0.343
at k<=6, no downward trend, and the planted-fault ladder agrees independently.
New identity, checked to 1.78e-15 over 200 configurations:
B(T,y) - sum_p B({t_p},y) = sum_{p!=q} Psi(tau_pq, y),
Psi(tau,y) = -(1/2)[D(0,tau) + D(2y,tau)].
It prices the obvious route exactly. Applying the closed k=1 inequality once
per pair needs sum_{p!=q} Psi >= (k-1) R(X)/400, whose left side depends only
on centre gaps and whose right side depends only on the atoms - so spreading
the centres sends the left to zero while R is untouched. The per-pair
decomposition is dead structurally, not for want of sharper constants, which
turns the ledger's measured verdict into a one-line argument.

a75fbae955e781bd3b3a99777979e3b0c7a559f2.subject: O9: the removable branch IS the divided series, kernel-checked
a75fbae955e781bd3b3a99777979e3b0c7a559f2.body: The step the borrowed bound could not reach.
files: sinh_taylor bounds |sinh t - t*P(t^2)|. Getting from there to sinh t / t
means dividing by |t|, and the bound RB/|t| blows up at t = 0 - which is
exactly where this branch is used, since 95 of the 2-D boxes touch y = 0.
The quantity is perfectly well behaved there; only the inherited bound is
bad.
shc_eq_tsum fixes that by dividing the series termwise BEFORE bounding:
(if t = 0 then 1 else sinh t / t) = sum' n, t^(2n)/(2n+1)!
for EVERY t, zero included. At t = 0 only the n = 0 term survives and it
is 1; away from 0 it is Real.sinh_eq_tsum divided through. Axioms:
propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound.
What is left of the truncation lemma is now a tail estimate - each term
at most 1/(2n+1)! on |t| <= 1, tail past N at most 2/(2N+1)! - which is
standard. It is out as project e7a77aa2, and this identity turns that
task from 'find a route that survives t = 0' into 'do a tail estimate'.
I attempted the summability step here too and stopped when it turned into
instance-resolution work rather than mathematics; the identity is the
part that was not borrowable and it is the part that is done.

Its hasSum_shc is my shc_eq_tsum in HasSum form - Real.hasSum_sinh
divided by t away from zero, hasSum_single at zero - which is independent
corroboration that the identity was the right hinge, since the prover was
given it as a hint and could have taken any route from there.
The tail is then a clean geometric comparison: factorial_pow_le gives
2^k (2n+1)! <= (2(n+k)+1)!, abs_term_le turns that into a (1/2)^k bound
on each tail term, and Summable.sum_add_tsum_nat_add sums it to exactly
1/(2n+1)! * 2 - the constant asked for, not a weakened one.
Verified here, not taken on report: statement byte-identical, scan clean,
builds under v4.33.0-rc2, axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound.

7c974567eaf39714964da8d595a807b87aa4256b.subject: k>=2: the anatomy of the binding configurations, and repulsion is load-bearing
7c974567eaf39714964da8d595a807b87aa4256b.body: Decomposing slack_k at the worst configuration found for each k says three
files: things the identity alone does not.
The cross term is a COST at every binding configuration, not the gain the
ledger's stacking route describes, and by k=12 it is comparable to the damage
(-0.102 against 0.142). The adversary declines the +1.7556-per-ordered-pair
relief that coincident centres would buy.
Incidence is not limited: one atom sits in the damage window of 10 of the 12
pairs at k=12, so the damage side scales with k essentially in full. Whatever
'at most one pair per damage window' bounds, it is not this.
Everything scales linearly in k - cross/k runs 0.0092, 0.0072, 0.0065, 0.0085 -
which is why the relative margin stabilises rather than collapsing, and which
means an argument losing a factor of k cannot work.
Repulsion contributes under 20% of the gain at those configurations, which
invites dropping it. It cannot be dropped: minimising with the term deleted
gives -0.2990 at k=1 and negative through k=8. The small values above are an
artefact of reading them off configurations chosen to bind the FULL slack.
PROOF-LEDGER's 'the repulsion-free route is arithmetically dead' therefore
holds, reached here from a different direction.

28eaee901519d87fc0500e042281e0aabbe6bfd5.subject: O9: the creative shortcut is measured and rejected, and the real seam lands
28eaee901519d87fc0500e042281e0aabbe6bfd5.body: Tested the idea of collapsing qreIv_mem by reusing phiC, whose _mem lemma
files: already exists. The measurement kills it, and in the useful direction.
phiC's real part and qreIv disagree on all three sampled boxes, and qreIv
is consistently NARROWER - by about 1 percent on the widest
division beats generic complex division here. So reusing phiC would mean
regenerating against wider enclosures for the sake of a shorter proof:
more cells, less margin. Bad trade, and now a measured one rather than a
matter of taste. qreIv_mem gets proved.
O9Real.lean isolates what that proof actually needs, over plain reals so
it depends on nothing in the package: re_div_eq and im_div_eq give the
componentwise real and imaginary parts of a complex quotient, and
im_div_over_y is the removable branch - the identity showing that
carrying the division by y inside each factor, as imNumOverY and

c459b21c198a00c634c087413785017fe196f966.body: Every centre gap in the saved k=12 witness is a near-integer multiple of 2*pi
files: and the atoms cluster on the same step. That is the damage-window spacing: the
nine windows sit at gaps 6.182 ... 6.279, converging to 2*pi, and the adversary
needs its atoms inside as many windows at once as it can get.
Confining centres and atoms to c0 + 2*pi*Z and x0 + 2*pi*Z costs nothing:
At k=8 the restricted search finds a WORSE configuration than the free one,
and by k=16 they agree to 0.007 - the smaller space searches better. This is a
real reduction: the continuum of positions collapses to integers plus two
offsets.
The obvious follow-through fails. Uniform periodic occupancy - every p-th site
with centres, every q-th with atoms, offsets optimised - is benign at every
(p,q) tried: the best is +0.694 at p=q=2 against a binding ~0.24, three times
the slack, with the limits existing (0.8100, 0.7514, 0.7154, 0.6940 in k) but
in the wrong place. The binding configurations use the lattice with IRREGULAR
occupancy and mixed depths, so k -> infinity does not reduce to a small
periodic cell, and the combinatorics of which sites are occupied is carrying
the difficulty.

16bb957d31690a5207c42cd0873cca46a3f3bb9a.body: PROOF-LEDGER records the k=1 result as 'strictly stronger than what the tree
files: carries (d >= 4, or n <= 3)', which reads as a strengthening of a published
lemma. It is not.
Both comparison lemmas are ours: retention_separated_of_le and
retention_le_three are in Zeta23Ext/EForm3/Main.lean. The upstream pin -
anthropics/zeta-23-lean @ 3635e74, the paper's own complete sorry-free
formalisation of Theorems A-E, 316 files - contains no occurrence of
retention, Eng, Kpair or Dam. The whole route is this lab's construction, so
the comparison is against an earlier version of our own lemma.
That makes the inequality novel in the weakest sense available: a statement
about a bespoke functional that nobody has proved because nobody has asked it.

approaches today. A public claim of 'we proved the k=1 retention theorem'
invites 'what does it give you?', and today the answer is nothing yet.

stranger: O9 went from never compiled to decide +kernel on 699 cells in a day,
and the first table was FALSE - refuted on 7 of 9 chunks - with this lab being
what found out, traced it to the leaf model, and rebuilt it. A negative result
about one's own artifact, found and published by the same party, is worth more
than a lemma nobody asked for.

k=1 stands at hardened grade and O9 beneath it is kernel-checked.

084f326db7fbbc7eada7e0838543ad59c6b77116.body: T1's uniform-lattice value was carried as an optimisation obligation. It is
files: not one. G4's withdrawal note closes "T1 remains an optimisation obligation
rather than a formula, but for want of a proof, not for want of a
counterexample"; for the uniform lattice at the critical spacing the formula
was already in the tree, in another file.
`centre_gas_row`'s summand at y = 1/2 is exactly `-4*kappa(s)`, with `kappa`
the kernel `counting_lemma.py` sums. `Kpair(u) = kernel(0,u)` is this
module's own `d_zero_is_minus_kpair`; `Dam(1,s) = -kernel(1,s)` wherever the
rectification is idle. `counting_lemma` already carries the Poisson collapse
`sum_{d in Z} kappa(2*pi*d) = 2*c2(0)`, valid because c2 is supported on
[-1,1] and vanishes at the endpoints. Splitting off d = 0:
The two modules had been summing the same kernel and neither said so.
The transfer is not formal, and the two conditions that make it legitimate
are pinned rather than asserted. The rectification `max(0, .)` would break
the band-limitedness Poisson needs, and it never binds on this lattice:
`damage(1, 2*pi*d) > 0` for every d in 1..200. Off the lattice it does bind
and the identity fails outright — at s = 0.3 the two sides differ by 3.6, and
that failure is pinned too, so the lattice identity cannot be read as global.
The first draft of the test asserted the identity globally and failed on
exactly that point.
Second consequence, and it runs the other way. `kappa(2*pi*d)` decays like
1/d, so `centre_gas_row`'s dmax = 200 default truncates a slowly convergent
sum. It approaches the closed form from below and never reaches it:
dmax        row            shortfall
The recorded 0.114045 therefore understates by 2.85e-4, and it understates in
the operator's favour — a smaller gas row reads as more slack. Corrected, the
ratio against the per-centre budget is 0.88041 rather than 0.878. Still below
1, so nothing downstream moves. Recorded in LANDSCAPE_RECORD alongside the
scan value rather than overwriting it.
What this does NOT do: discharge T1. T1 wants a bound over all centre
configurations; this is one spacing of one lattice. Lattice extremality still
has no proof — withdrawing G4 removed its only recorded counterexample, it
did not supply a proof. Measured grade throughout: double precision, and
2*c2(0) is quoted from counting_lemma rather than re-derived. Nothing here is
evidence about RH.

1fa392cae47da1a16120e60c0852e5a3f4eda606.body: T1 needs a centre-gas bound over all configurations. 084f326 gave the
files: uniform-lattice value in closed form, so if the uniform lattice is extremal
T1 follows from a formula. Extremality was believed and unestablished:
withdrawing G4 on 2026-08-18 removed the only recorded counterexample, which
is not the same as supplying a proof. This attacks it and fails to break it.
Free search: P-periodic configurations, m = 2..6 centres per period, 300
Nelder-Mead restarts over (P, offsets). Every m returned to the uniform 2*pi
lattice. The residual shortfalls are optimiser tolerance rather than
structure -- worst 3.6e-6, with returned offsets multiples of 6.2832 and
Structured families swept directly, no optimiser in the loop: alternating
gaps (strict symmetric maximum at the lattice), dimers (monotone in
separation up to 2*pi, the tightest tried costing 1.73), vacancies (every
density below, deficit diluting 3.59e-2 at 4 slots to 9.48e-3 at 13).
Two conventions chosen against the specific way G4 went wrong. The objective
sums d >= 1 ONCE, matching centre_gas_row, because comparing a two-sided
number against a one-sided one is the arithmetic that produced G4's 0.1200.
And it is periodic rather than finite-chain: a finite chain's middle row is
depressed by its own ends (0.099826 at k=21 rising to 0.110325 at k=101
against 0.114013), so charging a chain for boundary it does not have in the
problem is a second way to be wrong in the same place. That second choice is
why this module reads G4's pattern as 0.0666 where the withdrawal note reads
~0.0602. Different objects, recorded rather than reconciled away, and neither
is near the lattice.
The load-bearing test is not "nothing was found". A search that cannot
discriminate finds nothing too, so the discrimination is measured:
perturbations the optimiser resolves at 1e-6 move the objective by 1e-2, four
orders larger. test_the_objective_has_power pins it, and the calibration
against the closed form (-1.77e-09) and against the scalar kernel (4.34e-19)
are pinned rather than asserted.
This raises no rung and discharges nothing. L1-L6 in the module name the
limits: it is a search, the family is small and cannot express aperiodic or
multi-scale structure where a counterexample would most plausibly live,
Nelder-Mead is local, and everything is double precision with no enclosure.
Lattice extremality remains unproved and T1 remains open. Nothing here is
evidence about RH.

d97e9fef5b5c4fb69d6d2cc496eb3712bacf4a10.subject: frontier_math: turn the lattice-extremality search into an argument
d97e9fef5b5c4fb69d6d2cc496eb3712bacf4a10.body: 1fa392c searched and found no counterexample, which bounds the search rather
files: than the problem. This is the attempt to bound the problem, and it gets most
of the way. LATTICE-EXTREMALITY-ROUTE.md carries the reasoning; section 6 of
it is the honest part.
The per-centre cost has an exact structure-factor form. Poisson summation on
the inner sum turns an infinite sum over space into a FINITE sum over
frequency:
J = 2*rho*hhat(0) - 2*h(0) + (2/(mP)) sum_{j!=0} hhat(2*pi*j/P) |A_j|^2
with A_j = sum_p exp(2*pi*i*j*a_p/P). Verified against direct summation on
five configurations, three of them not lattices, residual below 4e-9. Holding
only at the extremiser would have made it a coincidence.
Three properties of kappa_hat then decide everything, and the middle one is
proved rather than measured. kappa_hat(xi) = 2*pi*c2(|xi|)*(1+cosh|xi|) is
supported on [-1,1], which is what makes the frequency sum finite. It is
positive inside, because c2 is the autocorrelation of g(u) = cos(sqrt2 u) on
|u| <= 1/2 and sqrt2/2 = 0.707 < pi/2, so g is strictly positive on the whole
of its support. And it vanishes at +-1, because the supports of g(u) and
g(u+1) meet at a point.
So every non-zero-frequency term is a subtraction, and dropping them gives
LP(rho) = -8*pi*rho*c2(0) + 2*kappa(0), decreasing in rho, equal to the
lattice value exactly at rho = 1/(2*pi). The 2*pi lattice attains it because
its only non-zero-frequency mass sits on that endpoint zero: it is the one
configuration that pays nothing. The dense side rho >= 1/(2*pi) is closed by
monotonicity alone.
Uniqueness comes out sharp. Equality forces A_j = 0 for j = 1..m-1, and
Newton's identities turn vanishing power sums into vanishing elementary
symmetric functions, so the monic polynomial with roots exp(2*pi*i*a_p/P) is
z^m - c and the offsets are equally spaced. The threshold matches exactly: the
band [-1,1] and the density 1/(2*pi) make the constrained modes precisely
j = 1..m-1, which is precisely the Newton condition.
What that yields, stated with its hypotheses rather than without them: for a
P-periodic configuration with rho >= 1/(2*pi) (H1) and K_1 <= 0 at every
non-zero difference (H2), J <= -4*c2(0) + 2*kappa(0), with equality iff
rho = 1/(2*pi) and T is a translate of the 2*pi lattice. H2 holds for the
extremiser: clip_is_idle_on_lattice(5000) = -6.36e-10, and 2*pi sits mid-band,
about 0.75 from the nearest sign change of K_1.
Four gaps, and the first two are not technicalities. GAP A, the sparse side:
for rho < 1/(2*pi) the bound is not loose, it is vacuous, sitting at +2.15
against a true value of -0.043 at rho*2*pi = 0.4. This is where the work is.
GAP B, the rectification: f = -kappa + K_1^+ exactly, the argument bounds
J_kappa rather than J, and the difference is 8.3e-2 for a mildly uneven pair
and 4.8e-1 for three centres. It reduces to a concrete one-dimensional
feasibility problem: find v >= K_1^+ vanishing on 2*pi*Z minus the origin with
vhat <= kappa_hat, and H2 can be dropped. GAP C is periodic to general
locally finite, GAP D is writing out the Poisson justification.
Measured and not offered as an argument: 400 random configurations at
rho >= 1/(2*pi), many with the clip firing, breached neither the lattice value
nor their own LP(rho). Both gaps are pinned by tests that assert they are LARGE
rather than small, so neither can quietly read as a technicality.
Also fixes four em dashes I left in 1fa392c, which violate the house style for
prose this session authored.

7efd5064dd4c1760bbbf7ab4cbc212b9680beb2d.subject: frontier_math: gap B closes, and hypothesis H2 goes with it
7efd5064dd4c1760bbbf7ab4cbc212b9680beb2d.body: d97e9fe reduced the rectification gap to a majorant problem and guessed at an
files: ansatz. The guess was wrong and the reason is worth keeping: there is a FOURTH
constraint the route document missed. The bound from g = -kappa + v is
LP(rho) + 2*rho*vhat(0) - 2*v(0), so tightness at rho = 1/(2*pi) needs
int v = 2*pi*v(0).
`(1 - cos x)*psi(x)` has the right zeros for free but also vanishes at the
origin, forcing int v = 0 against v >= K_1^+ >= 0. Infeasible, immediately.
What works is
because s >= 0, s(2*pi*n) = 0 for n != 0, shat = 2*pi*(1-|xi|)^+ is supported
exactly on [-1,1], and int s = 2*pi = 2*pi*s(0), so the tightness condition
holds for every multiple at once rather than having to be imposed.
Feasibility is then two one-dimensional inequalities, and both hold:
c <= inf khat/shat = cos^2(sqrt2/2)*(1 + cosh 1) = 1.4698290...
Margin 0.558. The supremum is at x = 0; the tail of K_1^+/s settles at
0.734916 by x = 3000. The infimum is the limit at xi -> 1 and is closed form,
because c2 vanishes linearly there with slope -cos^2(sqrt2/2).
So g = -kappa + K_1(0)*s dominates f everywhere, has ghat <= 0 everywhere, and
agrees with f at every lattice difference. H2 is gone: section 5 now holds for
EVERY configuration at rho >= 1/(2*pi), not only clip-idle ones. The bound
LP_v(rho) = LP(rho) + 2c(2*pi*rho - 1) still equals the lattice value at the
critical density for any admissible c, and stays decreasing because that needs
only c < 2*c2(0) = 1.6985, which the whole admissible interval satisfies.
Uniqueness survives: ghat < 0 strictly on (0,1), so the Newton argument runs
unchanged.
H2 is still true of the lattice, and now for a stated reason rather than a
table of values:
K_1's 1/x^2 asymptotic has two sources. The endpoints of c2 at w = +-1 give
2*c2'(1-)*cosh(1)*cos(x); the kink at w = 0 gives -2*c2'(0+), which does not
oscillate. Both slopes are -cos^2(sqrt2/2), so at x = 2*pi*n the cosine is +1
and they combine to the constant above. It is negative precisely because
cosh 1 > 1. Predicted -0.6277706 against measured -0.6277713 at n = 5000.
Two recorded constants in d97e9fe were transcribed from a coarse scan rather
than from the closed forms and are corrected here (c_upper 1.4698299 ->
Measured end to end: 300 random configurations at rho >= 1/(2*pi), zero
violations of J <= LP_v(rho).
What this does not do. The two inequalities are verified numerically on a
finite range with a settled tail, NOT enclosed; rigor.py is the natural next
step and both are one-dimensional. Gap A, the sparse side rho < 1/(2*pi), is
untouched and is now the only real gap: there the bound is not loose but
vacuous, +2.15 against a truth of -0.043. T1 is not discharged, k >= 3 is
untouched, and nothing here is evidence about RH.

8a28a4faa3fb0fe68649f4f22faba7efe4bc3406.subject: frontier_math: gap A has exactly one route, and half of it is closed off
8a28a4faa3fb0fe68649f4f22faba7efe4bc3406.body: Attacked the sparse side. It is not closed. What is established is where it
files: can and cannot be attacked, which is a good deal narrower than before, plus
one method that silently gives wrong answers.
THE ROUTE IS FORCED. The bound 2*rho*ghat(0) - 2*g(0) is linear in rho, so a
bound covering every density needs a non-negative slope, and ghat <= 0
everywhere permits only zero. Hence
and then the bound is density-independent and closes gap A and the dense side
together. With g = -kappa + c*s + u and c = K_1(0) this is a problem about u
alone: u >= 0, u(2*pi*n) = 0 for n != 0, uhat <= M := khat - c*shat,
uhat(0) = M(0) = 4.9441838, int uhat = uhat(0). The headroom is EXACTLY
saturated at the origin, since M(0) and the required uhat(0) are the same
expression.
AT BANDWIDTH 1 IT IS INFEASIBLE, and not narrowly. Boas-Kac writes a
non-negative band-limited u as |h|^2 with hhat supported on [-1/2,1/2]. That
is exactly Nyquist for spacing 2*pi, so Shannon pins h to its samples at
2*pi*k, and the lattice zeros kill every sample but one. What survives is
u = |h(0)|^2 * s, a multiple of the same Fejer kernel gap B already used, and
uhat <= M caps it at 3.5076780 against the 4.9441838 needed. Short by 29%.
Open: whether bandwidth above 1 helps, since uhat may go negative outside
[-1,1] where M vanishes. Poisson already forces uhat(j) = 0 at every non-zero
integer, which makes the 2*pi-periodisation of u exactly constant. That is a
lot of rigidity for a function that must also be non-negative and vanish on
the whole punctured lattice, but it is not a proof either way, and this commit
does not claim one.
A METHOD THAT DOES NOT WORK, recorded with its witness rather than forgotten.
The obvious attack is a linear program over uhat with u >= 0 imposed at
sampled x. It is unsound here, demonstrated on the case whose answer is known:
at bandwidth 1 the LP returns 4.908534, exceeding the proved ceiling by 40%.
Its solution dips to -7.6e-4 BETWEEN its own sample points, reaches -4.2e-2
beyond them, and violates the lattice zeros by up to 0.781 past the last n
constrained. Sampling a continuum constraint at finitely many points relaxes
it and the optimiser finds every gap. The first version of this session's LP
was also under-constrained in a second way, imposing uhat(0) = M(0) without
the separate condition int uhat = uhat(0); it is only because the bandwidth-1
answer was known independently that either error was caught. The right tool is
an SDP enforcing u >= 0 exactly through Fejer-Riesz, with the lattice zeros
handled structurally by factoring u = s*q rather than by listing them.

exited before any answer came back. Zero of the five answers were used. The sharp case is
Turing.TM2ComputableInTime.natAdd: the cell wrote 545 lines for $11.97 and landed them, and

twenty-six minutes after submission with nobody left to read it. Proved twice, paid for twice.

answers in 12-19 ms anonymously. That prices two questions that were costing Opus attempts: does

until an org admin enables them. Alone it is unreliable -- it failed to elaborate twice on
Subgroup.normalizer_bot. Wrapped in a propose-check-repair loop against AXLE it landed a proof the
kernel accepts in 1.178 seconds. Aristotle answered the same statement in seven minutes with a

38a2d1e574a067dcf73cdcd93fbe352d937f4492.subject: hunt: the sharp window constant for the zeros of xi', and why higher derivatives are blocked
38a2d1e574a067dcf73cdcd93fbe352d937f4492.body: The paper of 2026-08-10 raised the unconditional proportion of zeros of zeta on
files: the critical line to 0.6725, solving the window-optimisation problem for zeta
itself (its Theorem D). Its Remark 7.3 applies the same machinery to xi' but
does *not* solve the variational problem there: it reports a flat window and an
unexplained quartic, and records that neither reaches Wu's unconditional
This hunt solves it. The sharp constant is 0.86864150052976706411... for zeros
of xi' that are simple and on the critical line, 0.93432075... for distinct
zeros, attained at lambda = 1. Two consequences: the paper's quartic was already
within 1.5e-6 of sharp (and the derived kernel independently reconstructs its
coefficients, predicting the argmax at (-0.0716, -0.2561) against the paper's
(-0.070, -0.255)); and no admissible window reaches 0.86957, falling short by
9.285e-4, which settles the paper's open comparison negatively.
Checked before being pointed at anything unknown: the instrument reproduces
Theorem D to 10 digits and the flat-window F(lambda) at three separate lambda.
The functional reproduces all four published constants of Remark 7.3 to every

published form factor; direct summation of the geometric series in -xi''/xi';

agree to 14 digits, the coefficient formula is checked exactly by Dirichlet
convolution over 1260 squarefree n, and Bian's 2008 thesis reproduces the same
k = 1 coefficients exactly from sixteen years earlier.

guessed: F_k for k >= 2 exists in an unpublished 2008 Rochester thesis with no

side of the explicit formula decomposes place by place as
-sum_p log p (Q_p(f) - ||f||^2) with Q_p = (1-1/p)||Phi_p f||^2 — a genuine norm
at every place, from coefficients only, with no zeros in any definition.
Reconstruction agrees with zeta.weil.explicit_formula_sides to 22 digits.
Where it dies, which is the result. Q_p - ||f||^2 is not of definite sign: 52 of
the first 60 places positive, 8 negative. The local norms do not assemble, so
local positivity is compatible with either sign of W. Filed under docs/09 §5.1
taxonomy item #5, finite approximants.

factors and never chosen: zeta and L(chi) mod 5 pass at 0.8284,

fail. Controls: swapped coefficients move the verdict 15 orders of magnitude;
against 300 random period-5 sequences all fail and DH sits at the 6th
percentile; lesion blindness at eps* = 0.184; the pass side keeps margin >=
0.343 across 60 Satake angles. The honest boundary is stated in the module's
own scope(): it tests the local Selberg bound, not "has an Euler product" — a
genuine degree-2 product violating Ramanujan is rejected.

the archimedean side is positive and grows like (1/2)log(t/2pi). The
mechanism asserts the two positivities compose.

(mechanism first, numbers second) is auditable.

compose into Re (xi'/xi) >= 0 on Re s > 1/2. It is false.

It carries every hypothesis the mechanism uses, and more of each:

real on the critical line          imaginary part 0.0
Re (Xi_a'/Xi_a) = 0 on the line    1.3e-51
scalar Euler product               truncation defect 3.1e-06 at 400 primes
EPP, Lambda(n)(n^a + n^-a) >= 0    min -2.0e-34 over n <= 200, two routes
Bochner min eigenvalue             +0.0166 vs zeta's +0.0053
archimedean term                   exactly twice zeta's, positive, growing
and its zeros are rho +- a, so Hardy's theorem alone puts infinitely many off
its own critical line: 4 zeros measured in [0.1,0.9] x [10,25], 0 sign changes
on the line there, Re (Xi_a'/Xi_a) = -998 where the mechanism says >= 0.

90d7addb49c4b552426b39acbf1e090ed5da5ef7.body: K2-TWO-SPECIES.md section 2 starred `far constant 0.6636 > 0.637` as a
files: depth-1 correction that `Wt_tail_le`'s constant does not survive. It does
survive, and two separate errors were stacked under one sentence.
`Wt_tail_le` (Counting.lean:93) is `Wt w <= (637/1000)/w for 1368 <= w`, an
inequality between two explicit rational functions of one variable. No depth
occurs in it, so it cannot fail at any depth. The depth-carrying lemma is
`Qim_far_sq` (FarField.lean:227), hypothesis `hy : y <= 1/2`.
And `1368 <= w = s^2-2` is `s >= 37.0135`, while `two_species.far_constant`
scans `[8, 400]`. Both starred sups are attained at s = 12.715 and 12.625,
i.e. w = 159.7 and 157.4, where the proved envelope `Wt(w)*w` is 0.7042 and
0.7054. Neither row was ever in conflict with anything proved.
On the range the constant is asserted on, an Arb pass at 96 bits through
`ball_field.D_enclosure` (adaptive cells, 45,030 evaluations) gives
enclosure cost of 1.00005 over the float scan. Depth ladder 0.5844 / 0.5937 /
0.6094 / 0.6318 at depths 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1, all holding. The constant
first fails at depth 1.0494 (measured).
What does break below depth 1 is the derivation route, which is the finding a
k >= 3 pass actually inherits: `Qim^2 <= y^2 Wt(s^2-2)` reaches ratio 1.00438
at depth 1 and holds asymptotically iff `4 sinh(y/2)^2 cos(1/sqrt2)^2/y^2
Not closed: s > 400 has no depth-1 enclosure, since the tail composes through
the very lemma that fails, so it is float-grade only. The table's other
starred row (no_damage's 28/5) was not examined and is recorded as a thread.
Recorded in harness/departments/review_ledger.py as claim
`k2-far-constant-depth1` with this run's white-box AttackOutcome.
`standing_reasons` still asks for a blind attack, which is the true state.

there was no generator item to remove; see HANDBACK notes_for_operator.
